rationale: Panatlântica processes flat steel (hot/cold-rolled, galvanized, galvalume and pre-painted coils, sheets, blanks and steel roofing tiles) and distributes it as a steel service center. Its revenue comes mainly from steel products, so it fits Steel, the same way GICS treats steel service centers.

Bioma Educação (formerly Bahema) is a listed holding that controls a group of Brazilian private K-12 schools (e.g., Escola Viva, Dual Florianópolis, premium local-brand schools), so its revenue comes from tuition, which fits Education Services.

Bradesco is one of Brazil's largest private banks. It has a national branch and digital footprint, and most of its revenue comes from conventional retail, SME and corporate banking. The Bradesco Seguros insurance arm is large but secondary to banking, so the company fits Diversified Banks.

Federally controlled commercial bank focused on the Amazon/North region. It does conventional banking and development lending and is the sole operating agent of the FNO regional fund, which makes it a geographically limited regional bank.

Banco do Brasil is a large, state-controlled, nationwide commercial bank with thousands of branches whose revenue comes mainly from conventional banking (retail, SME, corporate and agribusiness lending, funded by deposits), along with a wide range of financial services, which fits Diversified Banks.

company_name: BANCO DO ESTADO DE SERGIPE SA
rationale: BANESE is a state-controlled multiple-service bank (banco múltiplo, mixed-capital company) whose revenue comes mainly from ordinary deposit-funded retail and commercial banking, concentrated in Sergipe, so it fits Regional Banks.

company_name: BANESTES SA BANCO DO ESTADO DO ESPIRITO SANTO
rationale: Banestes is a state-controlled commercial bank owned by the State of Espírito Santo, earning most of its revenue from regular banking (retail and corporate lending funded by deposits) with a branch network concentrated in Espírito Santo, which fits Regional Banks.

company_name: BANCO DO ESTADO DO PARÁ S/A.
rationale: Banpará is the Pará state-controlled commercial bank, earning mostly from conventional retail banking, payroll and corporate lending through a branch network concentrated in Pará, so it fits Regional Banks.

company_name: BANCO DO ESTADO DO RIO GRANDE DO SUL SA
rationale: Banrisul is a state-controlled commercial (multiple-service) bank whose revenue comes mainly from conventional deposit-funded retail, payroll-loan and corporate lending, concentrated in Rio Grande do Sul, which fits Regional Banks rather than a nationally diversified bank.

company_name: BANCO DO NORDESTE DO BRASIL SA
rationale: BNB is a federally controlled multiple-service bank (banco múltiplo) that does conventional lending and banking mainly in Brazil's Northeast, with the FNE constitutional fund as its main funding source; that regional footprint fits Regional Banks rather than Diversified Banks.

Banco Mercantil de Investimentos is the listed investment-bank arm of the Mercantil do Brasil group. Its activity is described as financial product intermediation, financing, portfolio management and financial investments, mainly in Minas Gerais and São Paulo. That makes it an investment bank rather than a deposit-funded commercial bank, so it best fits Investment Banking & Brokerage, though only secondary sources and no revenue breakdown were found.

Banco Mercantil is a mid-sized, deposit-funded commercial bank based in Belo Horizonte (Minas Gerais). It offers current/savings accounts, payroll-deductible (consignado) loans and cards, mainly to INSS retirees and pensioners, which fits Regional Banks rather than Diversified Banks given its size and regional base.

company_name: BARDELLA S.A. INDUSTRIAS MECANICAS - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Bardella is still an active manufacturer in Sorocaba, operating under judicial recovery; its main registered activity (CNAE 2822-4/02) is making cargo-handling and lifting equipment such as cranes, plus machinery for heavy industry and installation of industrial equipment, which fits Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components.

Baumer manufactures medical-hospital equipment (sterilization systems, surgical center equipment) and orthopedic implants and instruments in Mogi Mirim, which fits Health Care Equipment; the CVM metallurgy label is outdated.

Excelsior Alimentos (formerly Baumhardt Irmãos, Santa Cruz do Sul/RS) makes and distributes branded processed meats (hams, sausages, mortadella, pâté) and frozen ready meals such as pizza and lasagna, so it fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

Monark's main activity, per B3, is making and selling bicycles (net revenue about R$16M in 2023), which fits Leisure Products because GICS puts bicycles there; most of its profit comes from financial income, not operations.

Cambuci makes Penalty/Stadium sporting goods mostly in its own plants: balls and footwear bring in about 80% of revenue and textiles/apparel 20%, and footwear (football boots, sneakers) is taken to be the largest single line, so it goes to Footwear rather than Leisure Products (balls) or Apparel; reviewer should confirm the balls-versus-footwear revenue split in CVM ITR/DFP filings.

Irani is an integrated maker of corrugated cardboard packaging, its largest revenue segment, plus packaging paper (kraft/containerboard) and minor resins, so it fits Paper & Plastic Packaging Products & Materials.

AXIA Energia (formerly Eletrobras, renamed Oct 2025) mainly generates power, mostly from hydro and wind, and also has a large transmission arm (about 37% of Brazil's lines); generation is the larger share of revenue, so it fits Renewable Electricity rather than Electric Utilities. Second independent pass proposed 55101010 (Electric Utilities).

CEMIG is a state-controlled holding for a vertically integrated electric utility in Minas Gerais (Cemig D distribution, Cemig GT generation/transmission, plus smaller Gasmig gas distribution); electricity distribution is the dominant revenue source and investment focus, so Electric Utilities applies.

company_name: CENTRAIS ELETRICAS DE SANTA CATARINA S.A
rationale: Celesc is a state-controlled holding company whose dominant business is electricity distribution in Santa Catarina through its wholly-owned subsidiary Celesc Distribuição; its generation unit (Celesc Geração) and gas distributor (SCGás) are minor by comparison, so it fits Electric Utilities.

company_name: CESP - COMPANHIA ENERGÉTICA DE SÃO PAULO
rationale: CESP, now a subsidiary of Auren Energia, generates hydroelectric power at the Porto Primavera (Eng. Sérgio Motta) and Paraibuna plants, about 1,627 MW in total, and sells that energy, so it fits Renewable Electricity.

Ampla Energia e Serviços S.A. (now Enel Distribuição Rio, the former CERJ, controlled by Enel Brasil) runs the regulated electricity distribution concession for 66 municipalities in Rio de Janeiro state, which makes it an Electric Utility.

FERBASA is a vertically integrated ferroalloy producer (it mines chromite and makes ferrochrome and ferrosilicon, mainly for stainless and carbon steelmaking). Ferroalloys bring in most of its revenue, while its wind energy and forestry/charcoal segments are secondary, so it fits Steel (ferrous metals).

company_name: COMPANHIA DE FIACAO E TECIDOS CEDRO E CACHOEIRA
rationale: Cedro Têxtil is a Minas Gerais textile mill making fabrics (denim, twill/brins and canvas/telas, about 168 million m² a year) that it sells to apparel makers, so it fits Textiles rather than Apparel.

Rede Energia is an Energisa-controlled holding whose dominant operating business is electricity distribution. It controls four distributors: Energisa Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Tocantins and Sul-Sudeste, so it is classified as an Electric Utility.

CPFL Transmissão (formerly CEEE-T, privatized and acquired by CPFL Energia in 2021) is an electricity transmission concessionaire operating substations and transmission lines mainly in Rio Grande do Sul, and GICS places electricity transmission in Electric Utilities.

company_name: ENERGISA MINAS RIO - DISTRIBUIDORA DE ENERGIA S/A
rationale: Energisa Minas Rio (the former Energisa Minas Gerais, merged with Energisa Nova Friburgo) is an Energisa group electricity distribution concessionaire serving end customers in Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro, which fits Electric Utilities.

Habitasul is a holding company. Its subsidiaries make most of their revenue by developing planned real estate communities (Jurerê Internacional and others): urbanizing their land bank, building projects and selling the property. Hotel management, rentals and the minority equity stakes in Irani are secondary, so the company fits Real Estate Development.

AXIA Energia Nordeste (formerly Chesf), an AXIA/Eletrobras subsidiary, runs both large hydroelectric generation and an extensive high- and extra-high-voltage transmission network in Brazil's Northeast; transmission is a large share of its revenue (about R$6.0bn from making the transmission system available in 2024), so this vertically mixed generation-plus-transmission utility fits Electric Utilities better than pure Renewable Electricity.

Companhia Industrial Cataguases, founded in 1936, is a vertically integrated maker of flat woven fabrics (spinning, weaving and finishing), with some private-label garment making on the side, so its main business fits Textiles.

The former textile maker Companhia Industrial Itaunense, renamed in 2018, now earns revenue from selling power from its small hydro plant (CGH Dr. Augusto Gonçalves, Itaúna/MG), which fits Renewable Electricity; however, its main registered tax activity code is renting out its own properties, and the revenue split could not be confirmed, so Real Estate Operating Companies (60201020) remains a credible alternative. Second independent pass proposed 60201020 (Real Estate Operating Companies).

Melhoramentos is a holding company. Its main business, through Melhoramentos Florestal, is making high-yield pulp fibers from its own planted forests for paperboard makers. That business brought in about R$150m of R$177m in consolidated net revenue in 2025 (around 85%), ahead of book publishing and real estate, so it fits Paper Products (pulp, paper & paperboard mills).

company_name: COMPANHIA PAULISTA DE FORCA LUZ - CPFL
rationale: CPFL Paulista is a publicly held electricity concession company that mainly distributes power in the interior of São Paulo state, serving 234 municipalities. That is the core activity of Electric Utilities.
Gerdau S.A. is Brazil's largest steel producer, making long and flat steel and special steels in Brazil and the Americas, and also mines its own iron ore, so it fits Steel.

CSN is a vertically integrated flat-steel producer whose dominant revenue segments are steel and iron ore mining (CSN Mineração), both of which fall under GICS Steel; cement, logistics and energy are smaller segments.

Karsten is a Blumenau-based textile manufacturer whose main business is branded bed, table and bath linens (soft home furnishings such as towels and sheets) sold through more than 7,000 retail points, which fits Home Furnishings better than generic Textiles.

Vale is a diversified miner, but iron ore and pellets made up about 80.7% of its 2024 net operating revenue (Form 20-F). GICS puts iron ore mining in the Steel sub-industry, and nickel and copper are minority segments.

unclassified_reason: Cobrasma (a former railcar and steel-castings maker) has had no manufacturing operations since May 1998. It is effectively a dormant company whose remaining activity is managing old labor liabilities and its real estate, including the Osasco head office, which was auctioned in 2024 to pay labor claims. No current revenue-generating business could be confirmed, so no sub-industry applies despite the 'FASE OPERACIONAL' status.
rationale: The company's own website and Revista Ferroviária both say Cobrasma stopped all manufacturing in May 1998, and no current operating business could be found, so it is left unclassified rather than placed in Construction Machinery & Heavy Transportation Equipment.

Grazziotin runs multi-banner retail store chains in southern Brazil (Grazziotin, Pormenos, Franco Giorgi, GZT, Tottal) that sell mainly apparel plus some housewares, with merchandise sales making up nearly all revenue, so it fits Apparel Retail; the housewares/home-goods banner (Tottal) is the reason confidence is medium.

Guararapes (GUAR3) is the holding/industrial parent of Lojas Riachuelo, whose fashion retail stores account for most revenue (the Midway Financeira credit arm is a minority share), making it an apparel maker selling mainly through its own retail chain, which places it in Apparel Retail.
Conservas Oderich is a Brazilian food manufacturer producing and marketing branded canned meats, vegetables, fruits, tomato products, sauces and mayonnaise, which fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

CAL (Lindenberg) develops and builds high-end residential towers in São Paulo. It earns revenue from selling residential units, recognized as construction progresses, plus fees for managing developments and construction, which fits Homebuilding the same way peer Brazilian incorporadoras are classified.

Mendes Júnior Engenharia is a Belo Horizonte heavy civil/infrastructure engineering group (CNAE: construction of bridges and other special structures; legacy works such as the Itaparica hydro plant), whose construction business runs through the group's Mendes Júnior Trading e Engenharia, which is in judicial recovery, so Construction & Engineering is its principal activity; current revenue is very small (about R$1–2M/yr from services and rentals) and is mainly backed by legacy construction claims, so confidence is low.
Braskem is the largest thermoplastic resins (PE, PP, PVC) and basic petrochemicals producer in the Americas, which fits Commodity Chemicals (plastics and petrochemicals).

Döhler, based in Joinville (SC), is a vertically integrated textile maker whose main products are bed, table and bath linens, curtains and home decor fabrics. These soft home furnishings fit Home Furnishings rather than general Textiles, though it also sells some industrial fabrics.
Raia Drogasil (RD Saúde) is Brazil's largest pharmacy chain, with about 3,000 drugstores in every state, and most of its revenue comes from pharmacy retail, so it fits Drug Retail.

Mundial makes and sells consumer products across several segments, but its largest segment is Personal Care & Cosmetics (Mundial nail clippers, scissors and tweezers; Impala nail polish), which points to Personal Care Products; the other segments are Eberle metal fasteners for apparel and footwear, Hércules/Mundial food-service cutlery, crafts and pump solutions, and the CVM label 'Têxtil e Vestuário' only reflects the old Eberle business.
Electro Aço Altona is a Blumenau (SC) steel foundry that makes and machines cast steel parts for industrial customers, and GICS Steel explicitly includes iron and steel foundries.

WEG is an operating holding company whose subsidiaries make electric motors, drives and automation equipment. Its largest segment, Industrial Electro-Electronic Equipment, brings in about half of revenue, and commercial/appliance motors add about 8%. That fits Electrical Components & Equipment (motors and generators), although the GTD segment (generators, transformers, wind/solar, about 36-38%) gives it some overlap with Heavy Electrical Equipment. Second independent pass proposed 20104020 (Heavy Electrical Equipment).

company_name: ENERGISA MATO GROSSO DO SUL - DIST DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Energisa MS (formerly Enersul) holds the electricity distribution concession for Mato Grosso do Sul state, which was recently renewed for 30 years, and it gets nearly all its revenue from regulated power distribution, so it fits Electric Utilities.

Eternit's core business is making fibre cement roofing tiles (about two-thirds of 2024 consolidated net revenue of R$1.16bn), alongside concrete roof tiles and chrysotile mineral mining (about one-third, mostly exported). Fibre cement makers such as James Hardie are treated as Construction Materials, which also fits the mineral side.

Eucatex is one of Brazil's largest wood-panel producers (MDF/MDP/hardboard from its own eucalyptus forests). Panels supply most of its revenue, with paints, laminate flooring, doors and partitions as secondary lines, which fits Forest Products (wood panels) rather than Building Products.

company_name: FIACAO E TECELAGEM SAO JOSE S/A - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: The former spinning and weaving company stopped manufacturing around 2013. A 2018 management proposal says that since then it has been renting out its own properties to meet its judicial-recovery plan obligations, and it added leasing of own properties (CNAE 6810-2/02) to its corporate purpose. Its subsidiary São José do Nordeste Participações e Empreendimentos Imobiliários also lists leasing of own properties as its activity, so the current revenue-generating business is property leasing, which fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than Textiles. Second independent pass proposed unclassified.

Investimentos Bemge is an Itaú Unibanco-controlled investment holding vehicle (a legacy of the Bemge privatization). Nearly all of its roughly R$238m in assets is equity, and its income comes from financial investments and holdings rather than banking operations, so it is placed provisionally in Financials as an investment holding. Second independent pass proposed unclassified.

Taurus Armas mainly makes firearms, especially handguns, and most of its revenue comes from the U.S. civilian/sporting market (R$1.67bn revenue in 2024 on 1.18m guns sold); GICS treats civilian firearms makers like Sturm Ruger and Smith & Wesson as Leisure Products, not Aerospace & Defense, and military/police sales are a smaller share.

Frasle Mobility (Randon group) makes auto parts for the vehicle aftermarket and OEMs: brake friction materials, brake, suspension, steering and engine components. That makes it a vehicle parts manufacturer, which fits Automotive Parts & Equipment.

Tupy gets about 80% of its revenue from structural cast-iron parts and contract manufacturing, mainly engine blocks and heads for heavy commercial vehicles and off-road machinery; MWM engines and gensets add the rest, so it fits heavy-truck and machinery parts better than Steel (foundry) or Automotive Parts.

company_name: GRUPO CASAS BAHIA S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Grupo Casas Bahia (formerly Via Varejo/Via S.A.; Casas Bahia and Ponto banners) is a Brazilian omnichannel retailer that sells mainly electronics and household appliances through stores and e-commerce, with furniture as a secondary category plus a marketplace and consumer credit. Its focus on electronics and appliances fits Computer & Electronics Retail; its mixed categories and marketplace also make Broadline Retail a plausible alternative.

Hercules S.A.'s registered business is making and selling cutlery and other tableware, which fits Housewares & Specialties. Its recent financials show revenue equal to gross profit (no cost of goods sold), and a secondary source describes the business as licensing the Hercules cutlery brand. A brand licensor is still classified by the products it licenses, so the sub-industry stays the same.

company_name: HOTEIS OTHON S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Hotéis Othon owns and operates a chain of hotels in Brazil. Its financial statements show hotels still operating while it is in judicial recovery (recuperação judicial), so it fits Hotels, Resorts & Cruise Lines.

Romi S.A. manufactures machine tools (CNC lathes, machining centers), plastic injection/blow molding machines and cast/machined iron parts. Machinery is the dominant revenue source, which places it in Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components.

Têxtil RenauxView is a textile mill in Brusque (SC) that makes fabrics for garments, an activity that fits Textiles; it has been restructuring its financial debt through an out-of-court recovery plan, and its current operating scale could not be checked.

company_name: INEPAR S.A. INDUSTRIA E CONSTRUCOES EM RECUPERACAO JUDICIAL
rationale: Inepar is a capital-goods group in judicial recovery that has historically made heavy equipment for power generation and transmission, such as hydro turbines, generators and electrical distribution and control equipment, and has also done EPC/assembly work. Its registered main CNAE is 2731-7/00 (equipment for distribution and control of electric power), which best fits Heavy Electrical Equipment, although current revenue is very small (gross revenue of about R$3.5M for 9M24, against R$6.1M for 9M23). Second independent pass proposed 20106020 (Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components).

Itaúsa is a holding company that co-controls Itaú Unibanco, holding about 37%; the bank accounts for over 90% of Itaúsa's recurring results, while its other stakes (Alpargatas, Dexco, CCR, Aegea, Copa Energia, NTS) are minor. Under the dominant-business rule it is therefore classified like Itaú Unibanco, as a Diversified Bank, not as a Multi-Sector Holding.

company_name: JOAO FORTES ENGENHARIA SA - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: João Fortes Engenharia is a Rio de Janeiro-based residential real estate developer and builder (incorporadora/construtora) that builds and sells residential units through SPEs; it remains operational under judicial recovery, and like other Brazilian incorporadoras (Cyrela, MRV, Even), it fits Homebuilding.

Kepler Weber is Brazil's leading manufacturer of post-harvest grain storage equipment (silos, grain dryers, conveyors) for agribusiness, matching Agricultural & Farm Machinery, which explicitly includes grain dryers & blowers; the CVM metallurgy label is outdated.

Light SESA is the electricity distribution concessionaire for 31 municipalities in Rio de Janeiro state (main CNAE 35.14-0-00 electricity distribution) and a subsidiary of Light S.A.; regulated power distribution to end users fits Electric Utilities.

Lojas Renner is Brazil's largest fashion retailer: Renner, Youcom and Camicado stores plus a digital channel, with apparel driving most retail revenue. Its Realize financial services arm is secondary, so the company fits Apparel Retail.

Trevisa is a holding company whose main business, after selling its fertilizer (2000) and forestry (2019) assets, is inland waterway transport of bulk cargo (pulp, wood, coal, fertilizers, soy) through its subsidiary Navegação Aliança, which brings in nearly all consolidated revenue (~R$158M); only a minor share comes from leasing its headquarters building, so it fits Marine Transportation.

Mangels makes industrial metal products. Most of its revenue comes from aluminum wheels sold to automakers, so it fits Automotive Parts & Equipment, even though it also has LPG cylinder, steel service-center and galvanizing segments.

Estrela is a toy and game maker operating since 1937 (brands include Banco Imobiliário, Detetive, Genius and Autorama). It is still operating under judicial recovery, and toys and games are leisure products.

Marcopolo makes bus bodies and complete buses (city, intercity, micro-buses through Volare) for transit and road operators, which are heavy transportation equipment rather than passenger cars, so it fits Construction Machinery & Heavy Transportation Equipment.

MAHLE Metal Leve is a Brazilian auto-parts maker. It makes and sells internal combustion engine components (pistons, rings, bearings), automotive filters and thermal management parts for OEM and aftermarket customers, so it belongs in Automotive Parts & Equipment.
Metalúrgica Gerdau is a mono holding company whose only operating business is Gerdau S.A., a steel producer that makes long, special and flat steel. Under the holding company rule, it goes in Steel.

Iguatemi S.A. (formerly Jereissati Participações, which absorbed Iguatemi Empresa de Shopping Centers in 2021/22) owns and operates shopping malls and makes most of its revenue from rent and parking, so it fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than retail (it is not a REIT).

Metanor is a petrochemical company in the Camaçari complex and controlling shareholder of Copenor (Companhia Petroquímica do Nordeste). Its business is making basic chemicals: methanol, and formaldehyde and its derivatives. Its registered main activity (CNAE) is chemical manufacturing, so it fits Commodity Chemicals.

Metisa is a steel products manufacturer in Timbó, SC. Its main business is making parts for farm implements, such as harrow and plow discs and soil-penetration tools, which fits Agricultural & Farm Machinery parts; smaller lines include hand tools, railway and road-implement parts, and washers.

Minasmáquinas is a Minas Gerais group of Mercedes-Benz commercial-vehicle dealerships (trucks, buses, vans, plus parts, service and Michelin truck tires); selling heavy commercial vehicles to businesses fits Trading Companies & Distributors, the same treatment as peers such as Rush Enterprises, rather than consumer Automotive Retail.

Suzano Holding is a single-business holding company whose dominant asset is control (via a voting agreement, ~45.7% of common shares per Suzano S.A.'s 2021 financial statements) of Suzano S.A., a producer of pulp and paper, so it is classified by that operating business as Paper Products.

Nordon stopped manufacturing capital goods around 2011. Its March 2026 financial statements show that its revenue now comes from leasing its own factory units (about R$3.5m a year), so by source of revenue it fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than its outdated metalworking label.

Dimed (Grupo Panvel, PNVL3) operates the Panvel drugstore chain in southern Brazil; most of its revenue comes from pharmacy retail, while wholesale distribution and Lifar manufacturing are minor, so it fits Drug Retail.

Paranapanema is Brazil's largest non-integrated producer of refined copper and basic copper products (cathodes, rods, drawn wire, tubes, bars, alloys) at Dias d'Ávila; it is still operating under judicial recovery with about R$562M in 2025 revenue, which fits Copper (primary and basic copper products).

SPTuris is the São Paulo city government's official events and tourism company: in its 2024 financial statements, about 98% of operating revenue (R$716m of R$730m) came from producing and running city events (Carnival, the F1 GP at Interlagos, the strategic events calendar), with only a small amount from the Anhembi venue, so live-event production fits Movies & Entertainment best.

Petrobras is a state-controlled oil company. It explores for and produces oil and gas, and it also has large refining, transportation and marketing operations plus gas and power activities, which matches the Integrated Oil & Gas definition.

Petrolusa is based in Fortaleza and makes lubricating oils, greases, solvents and thinners. It doesn't explore for or refine crude oil. GICS lists petroleum lubricating oils and greases under Commodity Chemicals.

Pettenati is a Caxias do Sul (RS) textile mill that makes circular-knit fabrics (cotton, viscose, polyamide, fleece and others) and sells them to apparel makers, which fits Textiles rather than Apparel.

Portuense, based in Belém, sold hardware from 1947, but its own website says it has focused since the 1990s on renting its own commercial spaces to small retailers, which fits a real estate operating company (leasing and management) better than the CVM building-materials label.

Alfa Holdings is a non-operating holding (now ~94% owned by Banco Safra) whose value comes from ~50% stakes in Financeira Alfa and Banco Alfa de Investimento, i.e., the mid-sized, deposit/CDB-funded Alfa banking conglomerate focused on consumer (payroll) and corporate lending, so it is classified as a mono-industry bank holding under Regional Banks.

company_name: MASSA FALIDA DA SA IND E COMERCIO CHAPECO
unclassified_reason: The issuer is the bankruptcy estate (massa falida) of the former meat processor S/A Indústria e Comércio Chapecó. It has no ongoing business: the court-appointed trustee is selling the remaining plants and paying creditors. This makes it an entity in liquidation with no activity.
rationale: This was formerly a meat and food processor (Packaged Foods & Meats), but it is now a bankrupt estate. Its only activity is selling assets and paying creditors under the Santa Catarina court's supervision, so no operating sub-industry applies.

Alpargatas makes footwear. Most of its revenue comes from Havaianas flip-flops and sandals (2024 net revenue was about R$4.1 billion), so it fits Footwear rather than the CVM label "Têxtil e Vestuário".

Seiva's own operating business is growing pine forests on land it owns in Santa Catarina and selling the logs (Forest Products), but most of its earnings come from equity income on a non-controlling investment in Gerdau Internacional Empreendimentos (steel).

Sondotécnica is a Brazilian infrastructure engineering consulting firm that designs projects and manages, inspects and supervises construction work (dams, hydropower plants, transport). This fits the civil engineering part of Construction & Engineering, where peers such as WSP and Stantec are classified.

company_name: WLM PART. E COMÉRCIO DE MÁQUINAS E VEÍCULOS S.A.
rationale: WLM is a holding company whose main business is its group of authorized Scania dealerships (Itaipu, Equipo, Quinta Roda and others), which sell heavy trucks, bus chassis, parts and maintenance to commercial customers; its cattle and coffee farms are a smaller segment, so it fits commercial-vehicle distribution (as with Rush Enterprises) better than consumer auto retail.

Tecblu (formerly Teka Tecelagem Blumenau, linked to the Teka group) made and sold face, bath and kitchen towels, which are soft home textiles that fit Home Furnishings. Confidence is low because CVM lists the issuer as PARALISADA and its current operating status could not be verified. Second independent pass proposed unclassified.

Telebras is the state-owned telecom carrier that runs Brazil's national fiber backbone and the SGDC satellite, and most of its revenue comes from multimedia communication (SCM) data and connectivity services sold to the federal government and as wholesale capacity, which fits Alternative Carriers (high-bandwidth fiber network and satellite services) better than an integrated telecom operator.

Oi S.A. (formerly Brasil Telecom) is a fixed-line telecom operator; it has sold its mobile business and V.tal/fiber assets, and its remaining operations are legacy fixed-line telephony and Oi Soluções corporate telecom/connectivity services, which fit Integrated Telecommunication Services. Confidence is medium because a 2025–2026 bankruptcy (falência) decision means operations are shrinking under court supervision, though services continue.

The company makes titanium dioxide (TiO2) white pigment at its integrated sulfate-process plant in Camaçari, Bahia, and its mining segment is only residual activity from a closed mine; GICS places commodity-based pigments in Commodity Chemicals.

Unipar Carbocloro is a basic chemicals producer: it leads in chlor-alkali products (chlorine, caustic soda, hydrochloric acid) and is South America's second-largest PVC producer, which matches Commodity Chemicals (basic industrial chemicals and plastics).

Vulcabras makes sports footwear under its own Olympikus brand and the Mizuno and Under Armour brands in Brazil; sports footwear brings in more than 80% of revenue, and apparel and accessories are minor, so it fits Footwear.

Iochpe-Maxion makes wheels (Maxion Wheels) and structural components (Maxion Structural Components) for automakers, and nearly all of its revenue comes from these, so it fits Automotive Parts & Equipment; its railway business (Amsted-Maxion) is a minority stake counted under the equity method.

Azevedo & Travassos S.A. is a heavy civil engineering and construction contractor working on infrastructure such as sanitation networks and roads (Azevedo & Travassos Infraestrutura) and on oil and gas construction and assembly for Petrobras (Heftos), which makes Construction & Engineering the fit; its oil and gas production business has been spun off as Azevedo & Travassos Energia (AZTE3).

Wetzel S.A. (Joinville/SC) mainly makes cast and machined aluminum (and historically iron) parts for truck, bus and passenger-car makers, which were about 75% of revenue versus about 25% from electrical installation and lighting products, so Automotive Parts & Equipment fits better than the coarse CVM metallurgy label.
Bombril makes and markets household cleaning products such as steel wool, detergents and cleaners, and it keeps operating while in judicial recovery (filed Feb 2025), so it fits Household Products.

Recrusul makes road equipment for heavy trucks: semi-trailers, refrigerated vans and truck bodies, tanker and grain trailers, and isothermal containers. Like peer Randon, that puts it in Construction Machinery & Heavy Transportation Equipment, but revenue fell sharply from R$74M (2022) to about R$1.6M (2025), so activity is now minimal.

Klabin is Brazil's largest producer of packaging papers (containerboard, cartonboard) and corrugated boxes/industrial bags; paper plus packaging make up about two-thirds of revenue and EBITDA, with market pulp about one-third, so Paper & Plastic Packaging fits better than Paper Products.

Sansuy makes and sells flexible PVC laminates and films, plus PVC products made from them (tarpaulins, geomembranes, automotive coverings), which fits the plastics and films scope of Commodity Chemicals.

Aliperti S.A. is a former steelmaker that now holds rural land. Its revenue comes mainly from leasing that land for eucalyptus, from sugarcane partnership agreements (parceria) and from some crops it grows itself, so it fits Agricultural Products & Services, although land leasing gives it some real-estate character.

Padtec Holding (formerly Ideiasnet) is a holding with one business: its subsidiary Padtec, which develops, makes and sells high-capacity optical communication systems (DWDM transponders and amplifiers) for telecom networks, so it fits Communications Equipment.

Holding whose dominant operating business is Ipiranga's branded fuel distribution and marketing (the large majority of its roughly R$130bn in net revenue), with smaller businesses in LPG distribution (Ultragaz) and liquid bulk storage (Ultracargo), so it is classified as fuel marketing under Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing.

company_name: COMPANHIA DE ÁGUA E ESGOTO DO CEARÁ  - CAGECE
rationale: CAGECE is the Ceará state-controlled sanitation utility. Most of its revenue comes from water supply and sewage services to end consumers in Ceará municipalities, so it fits Water Utilities.

Investco S.A. is the concession company that holds and operates a single asset, the UHE Luís Eduardo Magalhães (Lajeado) hydroelectric plant on the Tocantins River (concession to 2035, controlled by EDP), so it is classified as a hydropower generator under Renewable Electricity.

DTCOM sells corporate communication, professional training and distance-learning (EAD) solutions to companies and institutions (B2B), so it fits Human Resource & Employment Services (employee training) rather than Education Services (which excludes employee education) or Telecom, despite the CVM label.

company_name: CIA. DE SANEAMENTO DO PARANÁ - SANEPAR
rationale: Sanepar is the Paraná state-controlled sanitation company whose revenue comes almost entirely from regulated water treatment/distribution and sewage collection/treatment tariffs, fitting Water Utilities.

CPFL Energia is a holding whose dominant business is electricity distribution (CPFL Paulista, Piratininga, Santa Cruz, RGE), supplemented by generation, transmission and trading, fitting a vertically integrated, distribution-focused Electric Utility.

company_name: CIA DE PARTICIPAÇÕES ALIANÇA DA BAHIA
rationale: Salvador-based holding whose reported net operating revenue (R$13.6m in 1Q26) comes from its subsidiary Aliança da Bahia Patrimonial leasing its own properties, including build-to-suit leases to Hospital Aliança and Assaí; it also holds insurance interests via ALBA Participação em Seguradoras/Cia de Seguros Aliança da Bahia and a small cattle/cocoa business, so the best fit is a real estate operating company, but the evidence is conflicting.

Bradespar is a single-company holding whose only material asset is its stake in Vale, a mainly iron ore and pellet producer, so it is classified with Vale's main business: iron ore mining, which GICS places in Steel.

company_name: INVESTIMENTOS E PARTICIP EM INFRA SA INVEPAR
rationale: Invepar is a transport-infrastructure holding that controls and consolidates GRU Airport (Guarulhos International Airport), alongside MetrôRio/urban mobility and two remaining toll roads; GRU Airport is its largest revenue contributor and main asset, so Airport Services fits best.

Motiva (formerly CCR S.A.) is a holding that controls toll-road concessions (~2/3 of revenue/EBITDA), plus urban rail/metro and airport concessions, so its dominant business of owning and operating highways and railtracks fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: ENERGISA SERGIPE - DISTRIBUIDORA DE ENERGIA S/A
rationale: Energisa Sergipe holds the ANEEL concession (Contract 007/1997, renewed to 2057) to distribute electricity to about 0.9 million customers in 63 municipalities in Sergipe, a regulated distribution business that fits Electric Utilities.

unclassified_reason: Dormant shell holding owned by GP Investimentos (GP Investments group), kept as a listed vehicle. It has had no operating investments since it left its former IT/tech-systems business in December 2004. Its corporate purpose is generic equity participation, it has no revenue, total assets are about R$0.1–0.14m, and it runs small recurring losses (about R$83k in 2018). There is no operating business to classify.
rationale: Caianda is a non-operating GP Investimentos shell holding: its purpose is generic, it has had no investee business since 2004, it has no revenue and its assets are negligible, so no GICS sub-industry applies.

company_name: CONTAX PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Contax Participações (formerly Liq/Atma) is a holding whose dominant operating business, through its subsidiaries, is outsourced contact center/customer experience and BPO services. It remains operating while in judicial recovery, with about R$334m of net revenue in 9M25. This fits Data Processing & Outsourced Services, which covers call center management.

unclassified_reason: CVM lists the issuer as pre-operational (FASE PRÉ-OPERACIONAL). Its corporate purpose is only a generic one: holding stakes in other companies. The sources found show no operating business, controlled operating subsidiary or revenue source to classify by.
rationale: This is a shell holding formed in 2000 when it was split off from Poconé Participações. Its stated purpose is only to hold stakes in other companies, and it is pre-operational with no evidence of an operating business, so no sub-industry can be assigned without guessing.

unclassified_reason: CVM lists the issuer as pre-operational (FASE PRÉ-OPERACIONAL). It is a generic shell holding, created in 2000 from a partial spin-off of Poconé Participações. Its corporate purpose is only to hold stakes in other companies, and no evidence shows an operating business, controlled subsidiary or revenue source to classify by.
rationale: Caconde Participações is a pre-operational shell holding with a generic purpose of holding stakes in other companies and no identifiable operating activity, so no GICS sub-industry can be assigned without guessing.

Saneago is the state-controlled water and sewage utility of Goiás, supplying treated water and sewage collection/treatment in 223 of 246 municipalities under program contracts, which is a core Water Utilities activity.

unclassified_reason: CRT's BR-116/RJ toll road concession (Além Paraíba–Teresópolis) ended on 21 Sep 2022, when EcoRioMinas took over the road. ANTT closed the transition committee in Oct 2022. The bylaws amended at the AGO/E of 11 Apr 2024 now limit the corporate purpose to managing the residual assets, liabilities, rights and obligations of the expired concession, including the economic-financial rebalancing claim. The company has no operating business left. It is a post-concession run-off entity, so no sub-industry applies, even though CVM still lists it as operational.
rationale: The company used to operate a toll road (it would have been Highways & Railtracks, 20305020). Since its concession ended in 2022, its only activity is winding down the leftover assets, liabilities and claims, so it has no current principal business to classify.

PROMAN is a member of the Consórcio Manso, which holds the concession for the APM Manso hydroelectric plant in Mato Grosso, and earns its revenue from hydroelectric generation, so it fits Renewable Electricity.

company_name: CIA PIRATININGA DE FORÇA E LUZ
rationale: CPFL Piratininga is a CPFL Energia subsidiary holding a regulated ANEEL concession to distribute electricity to about 1.9 million customers in 27 São Paulo municipalities, including Santos, Sorocaba and Jundiaí, which makes it an Electric Utility.

Biomm develops, produces (via PDPs with the Ministry of Health) and sells biotech drugs, mainly biosimilars such as insulins and monoclonal antibodies. Because these are protein-based therapeutics, it fits Biotechnology rather than generic Pharmaceuticals, but a lot of its revenue comes from in-licensed products, so Pharmaceuticals is a reasonable alternative.

company_name: TPI - TRIUNFO PARTICIPACOES E INVESTIMENTOS S.A.
rationale: TPI is a holding company whose main business is its federal toll-road concessions (Concer, Triunfo Concebra and Triunfo Transbrasiliana), and toll collection makes up most of its adjusted revenue, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Itaú Unibanco Holding is the largest private financial institution in Latin America, with a national retail, SME and corporate banking business in Brazil plus a diverse range of financial services, so it fits Diversified Banks.

company_name: COMPANHIA DE SANEAMENTO DE MINAS GERAIS
rationale: COPASA is a water and sewage utility that runs the municipal water supply and sanitation concessions across Minas Gerais and earns nearly all its revenue from water and sewage tariffs, so it fits Water Utilities; its control changed in the recent privatization, but its activity did not.

EcoRodovias is a holding company whose main business is its portfolio of toll road concessions in Brazil (about 11 or more highway concessions, such as Ecovias, EcoNoroeste and Ecoponte), with most revenue coming from tolls, so it fits Highways & Railtracks; its port and logistics businesses are minor.

Natura Cosméticos S.A. (CNPJ 71.673.990/0001-77) is the operating company of the Natura group. It makes and sells cosmetics, fragrances and personal hygiene products mainly through direct sales, which fits Personal Care Products.

Grendene is one of the world's largest footwear producers (Melissa, Ipanema, Grendha, Zaxy, Rider), so footwear manufacturing is its principal revenue source, fitting Footwear rather than the CVM textile/apparel label.

Dasa is Brazil's largest clinical diagnostics and lab-testing company; since its hospitals were moved into the Rede Américas joint venture with Amil (now 50/50 and deconsolidated), diagnostics brings in about R$2.1bn of R$2.7bn in quarterly gross revenue, which fits Health Care Services (lab testing services).

Bradesco Leasing is a Banco Bradesco subsidiary licensed as a leasing company (arrendamento mercantil under Lei 6.099/74), providing vehicle and equipment financial leasing funded by debentures, which matches GICS Specialized Finance, a sub-industry that explicitly covers leasing institutions.

company_name: SECME - COMPANHIA SECURITIZADORA DE CRÉDITOS IMOBILIÁRIOS
rationale: SECME is a CVM-registered real estate receivables securitization company (companhia securitizadora de créditos imobiliários), meaning it acquires real estate/mortgage receivables and issues CRIs backed by them, which matches real estate financing under Commercial & Residential Mortgage Finance (it is not a REIT); no primary source confirmed specific issuances or revenue. Second independent pass proposed 40204010 (Mortgage REITs).

Localiza is Brazil's largest vehicle rental company (RAC car rental and fleet management/GTF), with used-car sales (Seminovos) serving as fleet decommissioning of its own rental fleet, which fits Passenger Ground Transportation (explicitly includes vehicle rental).

EDP Energias do Brasil is a holding company that controls electricity distribution concessions (EDP São Paulo and EDP Espírito Santo), along with transmission lines, generation and energy trading; regulated distribution and transmission bring in most of its revenue, which makes it an Electric Utility.

Arteris is a holding company whose operating business is its controlled toll-road concessionaires in Brazil, earning revenue from tolls and operating highways; that makes it an owner and operator of roads (Highways & Railtracks).

Cosan is a listed holding and portfolio manager whose businesses span several GICS sectors, with no single business making up a majority: Compass (gas distribution, about 42% of R$44.0bn consolidated 2024 net revenue), Rumo (rail logistics, about 32%) and Moove (lubricants, about 24%) are consolidated, Radar (agricultural land) is also held, and Raízen (fuels/sugar-ethanol) is equity-accounted; this fits Multi-Sector Holdings rather than the outdated CVM sugar and ethanol label.

Light S.A. is a holding company for electric power businesses in Rio de Janeiro. Its main business is electricity distribution through Light SESA, which holds the concession for 31 municipalities and produces most of the group's results; generation and trading are smaller, so it fits Electric Utilities.

BR Malls Participações, now a wholly owned subsidiary of ALLOS that issues debentures, owns stakes in Brazilian shopping centers and earns its revenue mainly from leasing and managing them, which places it in Real Estate Operating Companies rather than Retail REITs because it is not a REIT.

TOTVS is Brazil's leading developer of enterprise management (ERP) software sold mainly as SaaS/cloud and recurring licenses. Its Gestão segment brings in most of its revenue (about R$1.1bn in recurring revenue in 4Q24 out of R$1.43bn total), with RD Station (marketing/sales SaaS) and Techfin as smaller segments, so it fits Application Software.

Equatorial S.A. is a holding whose dominant operating business is electricity distribution through its concessionaires (Maranhão, Pará, Piauí, Alagoas, CEEE-RS, Amapá, Goiás), plus transmission. Distribution and transmission make up most of its revenue, which fits Electric Utilities. Renewables, sanitation (CSA Amapá, Sabesp stake) and telecom are smaller.

Valid (formerly American Banknote) sells secure outsourced identity and transaction solutions in three areas: ID (issuing identity documents and driver's licenses and digital government services for Brazilian states, about 35-40% of revenue), Pay (making and personalizing payment cards for banks) and Mobile (SIM and eSIM cards for telecom companies), so with no single dominant product, the best fit is Data Processing & Outsourced Services rather than Commercial Printing or Technology Hardware. Second independent pass proposed 20201010 (Commercial Printing).

company_name: BRASILAGRO CIA BRAS DE PROP AGRICOLAS
rationale: BrasilAgro buys, develops, farms and sells rural land. Most of its operating revenue comes from producing and selling unpackaged agricultural commodities (soy, corn, sugarcane, cattle), so it fits Agricultural Products & Services; farm sales add a lot to earnings, but they are a smaller, uneven share of revenue.

CSU Digital's main business is CSU Pays, its card and payment-processing platform for card issuers, retailers and banks, which brings in about 60–70% of net revenue and most of its gross profit; that fits Transaction & Payment Processing Services, while the smaller CSU DX customer-experience/contact-center unit (about 30–40%) would on its own fall under Data Processing & Outsourced Services.

Dinâmica Energia S.A. is a small investment vehicle, about 99.99% owned by FIA Dinâmica Energia (Banco Clássico); it does not run an energy business itself and holds passive equity stakes in listed companies (for example, temporary holdings of Petrobras shares), so under the rule for investment vehicles it is classified in Financials as a closed-end-style investment company rather than as an electric utility.

Lupatech makes equipment, mostly for the oil and gas industry: made-to-order valves for oil and gas (MNA/Tecval), Petrobras-related products, mooring cables for offshore platforms and composite tubing for well lining; the Products segment is about 99.8% of revenue. A meaningful share comes from industrial valves for general industry (Valmicro/Mipel), so the case for Industrial Machinery (20106020) is weaker and confidence is medium.

Embraer designs and manufactures commercial and executive jets and defense aircraft, and provides aircraft services and support. All of its segments are aerospace or defense, so it fits Aerospace & Defense rather than the broad CVM machinery label.

Bradsaúde (formerly Odontoprev, same CNPJ) is the holding of Bradesco's healthcare companies following the April 2026 share merger of Bradesco Gestão de Saúde. Its main business is risk-based health and dental benefit plans (Bradesco Saúde, Mediservice, Odontoprev) that earn premium revenue, which fits Managed Health Care. Its minority stakes in hospitals and diagnostics, such as Fleury, are secondary.

AutoBAn is a CCR-controlled toll road concessionaire that operates the Anhanguera-Bandeirantes highway system in São Paulo, about 317 km long; it earns its revenue from operating highways, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: TRANSMISSORA ALIANÇA DE ENERGIA ELÉTRICA S.A.
rationale: TAESA builds, operates and maintains ANEEL-regulated electricity transmission concessions (~43 concessions, largest private player by RAP), and GICS places electricity transmission companies in Electric Utilities.
Cemig D is the regulated public-service electricity distribution concessionaire in about 97% of Minas Gerais, supplying captive consumers, so it fits Electric Utilities.

Cemig GT, a subsidiary of state-controlled Cemig, makes most of its revenue from selling electricity produced mainly by its hydroelectric plants (gross energy supply about R$5.1bn in 2024), with power trading alongside it; regulated transmission revenue (about R$1.3bn allowed annual revenue) is secondary, so the company fits Renewable Electricity better than Electric Utilities.

company_name: M. DIAS BRANCO SA IND E COM DE ALIMENTOS
rationale: M. Dias Branco is Brazil's leading manufacturer of branded packaged foods, mainly biscuits and pasta, plus flour, margarine, cakes and snacks, so it fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

Profarma is mainly a wholesale distributor of pharmaceutical and health products to pharmacies and other businesses: Profarma Distribuição made up about 84% of 2024 non-consolidated gross revenue, and the d1000 retail pharmacy chain made up about 16%, so it fits Health Care Distributors.

Positivo Tecnologia is a Brazilian manufacturer of PCs, notebooks, servers, monitors, smartphones and tablets sold to retail, corporate and government customers. Most of its gross revenue comes from hardware, while payment terminals and IT services are smaller and growing, so it fits Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals.

company_name: LPS BRASIL CONSULTORIA DE IMOVEIS S/A
rationale: LPS Brasil (Lopes) is a real estate brokerage and consultancy whose revenue comes mainly from commissions on selling new real estate launches and resale properties, which fits Real Estate Services.

Ecovias dos Imigrantes is EcoRodovias' toll-road concession company. It has run the Anchieta-Imigrantes highway system in São Paulo, under ARTESP regulation, since 1998, so as a single-asset road concession it belongs in Highways & Railtracks.

Tecnisa is a São Paulo-based residential developer and builder (incorporadora/construtora) whose revenue comes mainly from building and selling residential apartments and condominiums to homeowners, so it fits Homebuilding, the same sub-industry used for Brazilian peers such as Cyrela, MRV and EZTEC.

TLSA, controlled by CSN, holds the concession for the Nova Transnordestina freight railway (Piauí–Ceará–Pernambuco). It began test cargo runs in Dec 2025, so as a single-asset rail concession it falls under Rail Transportation; confidence is medium because operating revenue is still minimal while it ramps up from construction.

company_name: PDG REALTY S.A. EMPREEND E PARTICIPACOES
rationale: PDG Realty is a holding company for residential real estate developers and builders (incorporadora/construtora). It builds and sells residential units, and it is still operating while in judicial recovery, so it fits Homebuilding, as other Brazilian residential incorporadoras do.

company_name: IGUATEMI EMPRESA DE SHOPPING CENTERS S/A
rationale: IESC owns, leases and manages shopping centers (rent, mall management and parking revenue). It is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Iguatemi S.A. that issues debentures. It is not a REIT, so it fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than Retail REITs or the CVM 'Comércio' label.

São Martinho grows and processes sugarcane into sugar (mostly raw/VHP sold in bulk), ethanol and cogenerated power. Sugar and ethanol revenue are roughly equal (2024/25 net revenue R$7.2bn), so the company is classified by its integrated sugarcane agribusiness and market perception as Agricultural Products & Services rather than Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing for ethanol.

Even develops and builds residential projects (apartments and condominiums), mainly mid/high-end in São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul, and sells them to homebuyers, doing both the development and the construction itself, which fits Homebuilding, the category used for Brazilian builder-developers like it.

Santander Brasil operates as a large multiple-service bank (banco múltiplo) across Brazil, with commercial, investment, credit, real estate lending, leasing and foreign exchange portfolios. Its retail and corporate banking reach the whole country, which fits Diversified Banks.

CPFL Renováveis is a holding of operating renewable power plants in Brazil (wind farms, small hydro (PCHs), biomass and solar), with about 2.1 GW of installed capacity, so its main activity is renewable electricity generation.

Banco Pine is a mid-sized Brazilian bank that makes corporate (wholesale) loans and, more recently, payroll-deducted consumer loans (consignado), funded mainly by deposits such as CDBs and LCAs; it lacks the national retail footprint of a diversified bank, so it fits Regional Banks.
JBS is the world's largest animal protein processor (beef, chicken, pork, lamb, fish, plus value-added and branded meat products such as Seara and Pilgrim's Pride), which fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

JHSF is a high-end real estate group: residential development (~37% of LTM revenue to Jun/24), hotels and restaurants (~25%), shopping malls (~19%) and an executive airport (~10%). Real estate development plus malls make up most of revenue, but no single business line dominates, so Diversified Real Estate Activities fits best.

Metalfrio is one of the world's largest makers of plug-in commercial freezers and refrigerators sold to beverage, ice-cream and food companies, which fits commercial/industrial equipment manufacturing in Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components rather than consumer household appliances.

Heringer (controlled by EuroChem) makes, blends and sells NPK fertilizers to Brazilian farmers through 12 storage, blending and distribution units, with about R$1.4bn of revenue in 4Q24, so it fits Fertilizers & Agricultural Chemicals.

Fica (formerly CR2) is a small residential real estate developer in Rio de Janeiro/São Paulo that works through project SPEs, with revenue from selling units from inventory and new launches (e.g., Livre Alto da Boa Vista), which fits Real Estate Development; its stated move into residential rentals is not yet shown to drive revenue, and some Brazilian peers are classified as Homebuilding instead. Second independent pass proposed 25201030 (Homebuilding).

company_name: CIA ESTADUAL DE DISTRIBUIÇÃO DE ENERGIA ELETRICA
rationale: CEEE-D (now CEEE Equatorial) is the ANEEL-concession electricity distribution utility serving 72 municipalities in Rio Grande do Sul, including the Porto Alegre metro area, which fits Electric Utilities; control passed from the state to Equatorial Energia in July 2021, so the CVM 'ESTATAL' control flag is out of date.

Viver (formerly Inpar) is a São Paulo developer and builder that buys land, then builds and sells residential projects such as condominiums and apartment buildings. It still launches projects (Station Vila Madalena and Domum in 2023) and earns most of its small revenue from unit sales, which fits Homebuilding, the same sub-industry as peer Brazilian residential developers.

Log-In's main business is container coastal shipping (cabotagem) and feeder services, which make up most of its net revenue (about 85% in 3Q23), with the Vila Velha port terminal (TVV) as a smaller segment, so it fits Marine Transportation.

Paraná Banco is a Curitiba-based bank whose core business, since it refocused in 2018, is payroll-deductible personal loans (crédito consignado) to INSS retirees, public servants and military personnel, funded by CDB, LCI and LCA deposits; a monoline personal-credit lender fits Consumer Finance better than conventional retail or corporate banking.

SLC Agrícola is a large-scale Brazilian crop grower that farms soybeans, cotton and corn on owned and leased land and sells them as bulk commodities, so it fits Agricultural Products & Services (crop growers), not the sugar/ethanol activity in the CVM label.

company_name: EZ TEC EMPREEND. E PARTICIPAÇÕES S/A
rationale: EZTEC is a vertically integrated São Paulo developer and builder. Most of its revenue comes from developing, building and selling mainly middle- and upper-income residential units to homebuyers, so it fits Homebuilding, as Brazilian peers like Cyrela and MRV are classified; it also has smaller commercial and mortgage-financing activities.

Marfrig (now MBRF Global Foods after incorporating BRF) is a protein producer: it processes beef in Brazil, the US and South America, and BRF adds poultry, pork and processed foods. Meat processing and packaged foods make up most of its revenue, which fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

Banco Daycoval is a mid-sized Brazilian commercial (multiple) bank. Its loan book is mostly middle-market corporate credit (about 70%), plus payroll loans and vehicle financing, funded through deposits and other bank funding. That is conventional banking without the national retail footprint of a diversified bank, so it fits Regional Banks better than Diversified Banks.

Tegma's Automotive Logistics division brought in about 93% of 2025 gross revenue (R$2.57bn of R$2.77bn), mainly from moving new vehicles by road on car-carrier trucks, with yard, storage and pre-delivery services as smaller extras, so it fits Cargo Ground Transportation.

Helbor is a Brazilian real estate developer (incorporadora) whose revenue comes mainly from developing and selling residential apartment buildings. Under GICS, Brazilian peers that do the same (Cyrela, EZTEC, Even) are classified as Homebuilding, so Helbor fits there too.

MRV is Brazil's largest residential builder. It builds and sells low-income apartments, mainly under Minha Casa Minha Vida, which fits Homebuilding. Resia (US multifamily) and Luggo (rental) are smaller segments.

Minerva Foods is a beef slaughtering and processing company. It is South America's largest exporter of fresh beef and cattle byproducts and also has a processed foods segment, so it fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

Banco ABC Brasil is a multiple-service bank (controlled by Bahrain's Bank ABC) whose main business is lending and financial services to mid- and large-sized companies, with capital markets and M&A work on the side. It is a conventional deposit- and funding-based commercial lender without the large retail franchise required for Diversified Banks, so Regional Banks fits best.

Multiplan owns, develops and operates shopping centers in Brazil, and most of its revenue comes from leasing mall stores. It is not structured as a REIT, so it fits Real Estate Operating Companies; the CVM construction label is outdated.

Americanas is still trading while in judicial recovery. It runs a national chain of general-merchandise stores selling many product categories, plus a digital channel, which fits Broadline Retail (general merchandise and department-store-type retail).

company_name: GENERAL SHOPPING E OUTLETS DO BRASIL BRASIL S.A.
rationale: General Shopping e Outlets owns and manages shopping malls and outlet centers in Brazil and earns most of its revenue from rent and mall services, so it is a non-REIT real estate operating company; the CVM "Comércio" label does not fit what it actually does.

YDUQS is a holding company whose dominant operating business is private higher education (Estácio, Wyden, Ibmec and IDOMED in both on-campus and digital formats), with nearly all revenue coming from tuition, so it fits Education Services.

Algar Telecom (formerly CTBC) is a fiber-based telecom operator. It sells fixed-line, broadband and data services, mostly to businesses (61% of revenue) and also to retail customers, and it runs mobile services as well, so it fits Integrated Telecommunication Services.

SYN Prop & Tech (formerly Cyrela Commercial Properties) owns, leases and manages shopping malls, office buildings and warehouses, earning mainly rental and property-management income; it is not a REIT, so it fits Real Estate Operating Companies.

Moura Dubeux is an integrated residential developer and builder (incorporadora/construtora) of apartments and condominiums for sale in Northeast Brazil, consistent with the Homebuilding treatment of Brazilian peers such as Cyrela and MRV.

Dexco (formerly Duratex) earns most of its revenue, about 65-68% of consolidated net revenue, from its Wood division, which makes MDF/MDP wood panels and laminate flooring under the Duratex and Durafloor brands; GICS lists wood panels under Forest Products, while Deca metals/sanitaryware and Portinari/Ceusa ceramic tiles (Building Products) are smaller segments.

Trisul is a residential developer and builder (incorporadora e construtora) in metropolitan São Paulo that builds and sells apartments to homebuyers, which fits Homebuilding, the same treatment as Brazilian peers like Cyrela and MRV.

Tenda builds, develops and sells affordable residential housing units (Minha Casa Minha Vida segment) to homebuyers, fitting Homebuilding, consistent with how other Brazilian residential developers like MRV are classified.

J. Macêdo mills wheat and makes and sells branded packaged foods, including wheat flour, pasta, cake mixes and cookies, under the Dona Benta, Sol, Petybon, Brandini and Boa Sorte brands, which fits Packaged Foods & Meats.

company_name: NEXPE PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Nexpe Participações appears to be PDG Realty under a new name. It is a holding company in judicial recovery whose operating subsidiaries develop and build residential housing for sale, so it follows how Brazilian residential developers are classified in GICS: Homebuilding. Second independent pass proposed 60201040 (Real Estate Services).

VIX Logística (Grupo Águia Branca) is a road-based logistics operator. Most of its revenue comes from road freight in its Dedicated Logistics and Automotive Logistics segments, where Automotive Logistics carries new vehicles and bus chassis; the 2024 statements show cargo transport as the largest revenue line, with fleet rental/management and passenger charter as smaller segments, so it fits Cargo Ground Transportation.

Eneva is a vertically integrated "reservoir-to-wire" company: it produces its own onshore natural gas, mainly in the Parnaíba basin, and most of that gas goes to its own power plants, while most consolidated revenue comes from thermal power generation (gas and coal plants such as the Parnaíba complex and Jaguatirica II) sold into the national grid (SIN), so it is a non-renewable Independent Power Producer rather than an E&P company.

Nutriplant (NUTR3) develops and makes specialty fertilizers: foliar fertilizers, micronutrients and inoculants, plus inorganic chemical raw materials, mainly for agriculture, so it fits Fertilizers & Agricultural Chemicals despite the CVM 'Agricultura (Açúcar, Álcool e Cana)' label; its extrajudicial recovery proceeding does not stop it operating.

company_name: OSX BRASIL S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: OSX Brasil was set up as a shipbuilder, but that business is now dormant; its only operating revenue comes from subsidiary OSX Açu leasing quay and land areas (and granting surface rights) on its 3.2 million m² site (the UCN Açu shipyard) inside the Porto do Açu port complex, which best fits Marine Ports & Services. Second independent pass proposed 60201020 (Real Estate Operating Companies).

Direcional is a vertically integrated developer and builder of residential housing units sold to households, mainly low- and middle-income (Minha Casa Minha Vida/Riva). That makes Homebuilding the fit, consistent with how Brazilian peers such as MRV and Cury are treated.

CELGPAR is the Goiás state energy holding. Its distribution business (CELG D) was sold in 2017 and its CELG T transmission assets in 2021, and in 2025 EDP bought its remaining transmission subsidiaries (Firminópolis and Lago Azul), so what is left is the hydro concessions it runs directly (UHE Rochedo and São Domingos, sold under the quota regime) plus stakes in hydro/solar SPEs, which fits renewable electricity generation. Second independent pass proposed unclassified.

Hypera (formerly Hypermarcas) is Brazil's largest pharmaceutical company. It develops, makes and sells prescription drugs, OTC medicines, generics/similars and consumer-health products, having sold its personal-care/consumer-goods businesses in 2017-2018, so it fits Pharmaceuticals.

Veste S.A. (formerly Restoque) owns and designs the Le Lis, Dudalina, John John and Bo.Bô apparel brands. Most of its revenue comes from its own chain of about 175 stores (Q3 2026 retail R$278M vs wholesale R$80M), so it fits Apparel Retail as an apparel maker that sells mainly through its own stores.

Banco RCI Brasil is the captive finance arm of Renault and Nissan in Brazil (Mobilize Financial Services), and most of its portfolio is auto loans and leasing made directly to end consumers, with dealer floor-plan lending as a smaller part, so it fits Consumer Finance rather than a deposit-led bank.

Alupar is a private holding company that controls electricity transmission concessions (roughly 77–78% of regulatory net revenue) and smaller hydro, wind and solar generation assets, so its dominant business is electricity transmission, which falls under Electric Utilities.

B3 is Brazil's financial market infrastructure provider. It runs the exchange and OTC trading, clearing, central depository and registration, and sells data/technology services. Most of its revenue comes from exchange and post-trade fees, which fits Financial Exchanges & Data.

Renova Energia makes most of its revenue (R$259.2m net revenue in 2024) by generating and selling wind power from its Alto Sertão III wind complex in Bahia, which makes it a renewable electricity producer.

PDG Companhia Securitizadora is the PDG group's securitization vehicle: it acquires real estate receivables and issues Certificados de Recebíveis Imobiliários (CRIs) backed by them, which is real estate financing and fits Commercial & Residential Mortgage Finance, not a REIT; it is in judicial recovery but still services outstanding CRIs.

Cielo is a licensed payment institution and one of Brazil's leading merchant acquirers. Its revenue comes from card transaction capture, processing and settlement, plus related prepayment of receivables, which fits Transaction & Payment Processing Services.

Ferrovia Norte Sul S.A. (FNS) is a VLI subsidiary based in São Luís that holds the subconcession of the North-South Railway's northern section and earns its revenue from rail freight transport. That makes it a rail freight operator, so it fits Rail Transportation.

company_name: CONCESSIONARIA DE RODOVIAS DO INTERIOR PAULISTA S/A
rationale: Intervias is the Arteris-controlled toll road concessionaire running about 380 km of highways with 9 toll plazas in north-central São Paulo state; a single-activity road concession fits Highways & Railtracks.

Fleury is one of Brazil's leading diagnostic medicine providers (clinical lab testing and imaging via patient service units ~68% and B2B lab/Pardini lab-to-lab ~23% of gross revenue), which fits Health Care Services (lab testing services) rather than Health Care Facilities, as hospital/new businesses are a minor share.

ECS is EcoRodovias' sub-holding that controls the group's toll-road concessions (e.g., Ecovias dos Imigrantes, Ecovias Raposo Castello) and raises debentures to fund them; as a mono-holding of highway concession operators it fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: ENERGISA PARAÍBA - DISTRIBUIDORA DE ENERGIA S/A
rationale: Energisa Paraíba (formerly SAELPA) is the regulated electricity distribution concessionaire for the state of Paraíba, serving about 1.4 million consumer units in 222 municipalities, which places it in Electric Utilities.

Arteris subsidiary holding the federal toll-road concession for BR-116 (Régis Bittencourt, São Paulo–Curitiba, ~402 km), earning toll revenue from operating and maintaining the highway — a single-asset road concession, hence Highways & Railtracks.

Autopista Planalto Sul (Arteris Planalto Sul) runs a federal toll road concession regulated by ANTT on the BR-116 between Curitiba/PR and the SC/RS border, with five toll plazas, so it fits Highways & Railtracks as a single-asset toll road concession.

Autopista Fernão Dias is a single-asset concession: it holds the toll road concession for the BR-381 (Fernão Dias highway) between São Paulo and Minas Gerais, formerly under Arteris and being acquired by Motiva. Because it owns and operates a toll road, it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Autopista Litoral Sul (Arteris Litoral Sul) holds the federal ANTT toll-road concession for BR-116/376/PR and BR-101/SC between Curitiba and Florianópolis, so it fits Highways & Railtracks as a single-asset toll-road operator.

Autopista Fluminense is the Arteris-controlled federal toll-road concessionaire operating BR-101/RJ (Ponte Rio-Niterói to the RJ/ES border), earning toll revenue as a road owner/operator, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: MILLS LOCAÇÃO, SERVIÇOS E LOGÍSTICA S.A.
rationale: Mills is Brazil's largest B2B equipment rental company (aerial work platforms ~47% of revenue, yellow-line heavy machinery ~26%, formwork/shoring, forklifts), which GICS places in Trading Companies & Distributors as industrial machinery rental to businesses.

JSL (a Simpar subsidiary) is Brazil's largest road logistics company: about 45-47% of net revenue comes from road freight, about 34% from dedicated logistics operations and about 7% from urban distribution, all mainly truck-based, so Cargo Ground Transportation fits best.

Marisa Lojas operates one of Brazil's largest chains of women's fashion stores, selling apparel, lingerie, footwear and accessories; retail is its dominant revenue source, while its financial services arm (M Bank) is ancillary, so it fits Apparel Retail.

Single-asset toll road concession that has operated the Corredor Dom Pedro highway system (SP-065 and connecting roads) in São Paulo state under an ARTESP concession since April 2009, so it is an owner/operator of roads.

company_name: CONCESSÃO METROVIÁRIA DO RIO DE JANEIRO SA
rationale: MetrôRio holds the public concession to operate and maintain Rio de Janeiro's subway Lines 1, 2 and 4, and most of its revenue comes from passenger fares, so it is classified as passenger rail transportation.

company_name: AFLUENTE TRANSMISSÃO DE ENERGIA ELETRICA S/A
rationale: Afluente T is a Neoenergia-controlled electricity transmission concessionaire operating substations and ~489 km of transmission lines in Bahia; GICS places electricity transmission companies in Electric Utilities.

PRIO (formerly Petro Rio) is an independent upstream company that acquires, redevelops and operates offshore producing oil fields in Brazil (e.g., Frade, Peregrino, Albacora Leste, Polvo/Tubarão Martelo); nearly all its revenue comes from selling crude oil and has no significant refining or marketing arm, so it fits Oil & Gas Exploration & Production.

Transbrasiliana is a Triunfo group subsidiary holding the federal ANTT concession for the São Paulo stretch of the BR-153 highway (Icém to Ourinhos), earning toll revenue from plazas on that road, so as a single-asset toll road concession it fits Highways & Railtracks.

CART is a special-purpose company that holds the ARTESP concession for the Raposo Tavares highway corridor in São Paulo state, and nearly all its revenue comes from toll collection, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Azzas 2154 (Arezzo&Co–Grupo Soma merger) designs, sources and sells fashion brands (Farm, Animale, Hering, Reserva, Arezzo, Schutz); about two-thirds of 2024 gross revenue (~R$14.2bn) came from apparel and 32% from footwear, so apparel is the main activity. Sales are split across own stores, franchises, multibrand wholesale and digital, which makes it a branded apparel maker rather than mainly a retailer (Apparel Retail 25504010 is the alternative).

ALLOS (formerly Aliansce Sonae, merged with brMalls) owns, leases and manages a large portfolio of Brazilian shopping centers, earning mainly rental and mall management revenue; it is not a REIT structure, so it fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than Retail REITs or the CVM retail label.

company_name: CONCESSIONÁRIA DAS RODOVIAS AYRTON SENNA E CARVALHO PINTO S/A-ECOPISTAS
rationale: Ecopistas (now Ecovias Leste Paulista, an EcoRodovias subsidiary) is a single-asset toll road concession operating the Ayrton Senna–Carvalho Pinto highway system in São Paulo, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Magazine Luiza is a large Brazilian multichannel retailer with physical stores, e-commerce and a marketplace (Magalu). It sells a wide range of consumer discretionary goods, mainly electronics, appliances and furniture, so Broadline Retail fits better than a single specialty retail category.

company_name: QUALICORP CONSULTORIA E CORRETORA DE SEGUROS S.A.
rationale: Qualicorp is Brazil's largest administrator of collective (affinity-group/adhesion and corporate) health benefit plans regulated by ANS, earning mainly administration fees plus brokerage commissions on health plans; as a health-benefit-plan administrator it fits Managed Health Care (health benefit plans), though it does not underwrite risk itself, making Insurance Brokers the main alternative.

company_name: MASSA FALIDA DA BRASIL PHARMA SA
unclassified_reason: Bankruptcy estate (massa falida): Brasil Pharma's falência was decreed in 2019, its shares were suspended from B3 and its CVM registration was suspended for non-filing; the former drugstore chain (Farmais, Guararapes, Mais Econômica) has no ongoing operating activity. Historically it would have been Drug Retail (30101010).
rationale: Former pharmacy-chain holding now in bankruptcy liquidation with no operating business, so no current sub-industry applies.

Technos S.A. designs, assembles (Manaus) and sells wristwatches under brands like Technos, Euro, Mormaii and Fossil licenses, mainly through wholesale to retailers. Watch makers fall under Apparel, Accessories & Luxury Goods, even though the CVM label says Commerce.

ViaRondon is a single-asset toll road concession under ARTESP. It operates the SP-300 Marechal Rondon highway in western São Paulo state, around Bauru and Lins, and earns its revenue from tolls, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Inbrands is a Brazilian fashion group that owns and designs apparel brands (Ellus, Richards, Salinas, VR, Alexandre Herchcovitch) and sells them through multibrand wholesale, franchises, its own stores and e-commerce. Because the business is built around owning brands and revenue is split across channels rather than dominated by its own retail stores, it fits Apparel, Accessories & Luxury Goods better than Apparel Retail.

MLog (ex-Manabi) is a holding whose operating revenue comes from shipping subsidiaries: Asgaard Bourbon Navegação (offshore support), Companhia de Navegação da Amazônia (river navigation) and NSN/Columbus (inland and cabotage). Its Morro do Pilar iron-ore project and Linhares port project are still pre-operational, so Marine Transportation fits best; offshore support (Oil & Gas Equipment & Services) is an alternative if it turns out to be the largest segment. Second independent pass proposed 10101020 (Oil & Gas Equipment & Services).
Empreendimentos Pague Menos (PGMN3) operates one of Brazil's largest retail pharmacy chains (Pague Menos and Extrafarma), with nearly all revenue from drugstore retail sales, fitting Drug Retail.

Banco BTG Pactual is an investment bank with revenue spread across several large lines (corporate lending and business banking, sales and trading, investment banking, asset management and wealth management) and no single dominant one, which matches the definition of Diversified Capital Markets rather than a retail-focused diversified bank.

Hidrovias do Brasil earns most of its revenue from carrying grain, iron ore and fertilizers by barge on inland waterways in its Northern (Tapajós/Amazon) and Southern (Paraguay-Paraná) corridors; it also runs related transshipment and port terminals, so the business is mainly waterborne cargo transport, which fits Marine Transportation rather than Marine Ports & Services.

company_name: CACHOEIRA PAULISTA TRANSMISSORA DE ENERGIA SA
rationale: Single-asset electricity transmission concessionaire (ANEEL Concession Contract 84/2002, 500 kV Tijuco Preto–Cachoeira Paulista line and Lorena substation) earning regulated RAP revenue; electricity transmission is classified as Electric Utilities.

company_name: CONC RODOVIAS DO TIETÊ S.A.- EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Single-asset toll road concessionaire operating the Corredor Leste of the Rodovia Marechal Rondon and connected highways in São Paulo state under an ARTESP concession running to 2039 (the restructuring did not interrupt operations), so it is classified as an owner/operator of roads.

Unicasa makes planned/modular furniture (Dell Anno, Favorita, New, Casa Brasileira) at its Bento Gonçalves factory and sells it through exclusive dealer stores, so its principal activity is furniture manufacturing, which places it in Home Furnishings.
Eldorado Brasil makes and sells bleached eucalyptus pulp at its Três Lagoas (MS) mill, about 1.7 Mt a year, using its own eucalyptus plantations; GICS puts pulp mills in Paper Products.
