Ferreira Gomes Energia is Alupar's single-asset concession company. It owns and operates the 252 MW Ferreira Gomes hydroelectric plant on the Araguari River in Amapá, so it is a hydropower generator and fits Renewable Electricity.

Light Energia is the generation subsidiary of Light S.A. It operates five hydroelectric plants (about 870 MW) and two pumping stations in Rio de Janeiro/São Paulo, and its transmission assets are minor, so hydropower generation fits Renewable Electricity.

BB Seguridade is an insurance holding whose earnings come from Brasilseg (life, rural and P&C insurance), Brasilprev (pension/annuities), Brasilcap and Brasildental, plus BB Corretora, which distributes the group's products; because its insurance business spans life, P&C and pension lines, Multi-line Insurance fits best.

Rodovias das Colinas is a single-asset toll road concessionaire in São Paulo state's concession program. It operates about 307 km of highways and earns its revenue mainly from tolls, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Iguá Saneamento (formerly CAB Ambiental), controlled by IG4 Capital, is a holding company whose subsidiaries run water supply and sewage systems under concessions and PPPs in 38 municipalities across six Brazilian states, so it fits Water Utilities.

Ser Educacional (B3: SEER3) is a private higher-education group running on-campus and distance-learning universities and colleges (e.g., UNINASSAU, UNAMA, UNG), with almost all revenue coming from tuition, so it fits Education Services.

Raízen Energia S.A. is Raízen's sugarcane subsidiary (registered CNAE: raw sugar manufacturing). It makes ethanol (including second-generation), sugar and bioelectricity, and trades energy. Ethanol and renewables likely bring in more revenue than sugar, and GICS places ethanol producers in Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, so that is the code chosen over Agricultural Products & Services. The revenue split is mixed and was not confirmed from a primary filing.

Ânima Holding (Ânima Educação) is a holding whose dominant business is operating private higher-education institutions in Brazil (e.g., UNISUL, ex-Laureate assets, medical schools via Inspirali), which fits Education Services.

Ambev, the AB InBev-controlled company, makes most of its net revenue from producing and selling beer in Brazil, Central America, the Caribbean, Latin America South and Canada; its soft drinks are a smaller secondary segment, so it fits Brewers.

LOG CP develops, owns and leases logistics warehouse condominiums and strip malls in Brazil, with most revenue coming from rent; as a Brazilian S.A. without REIT status, it fits Real Estate Operating Companies rather than the construction label CVM gives it.

Unidas Locações e Serviços (Curitiba) rents out vehicles and manages fleets: its registered activity is renting cars without drivers (CNAE 77.11-0-00), and its stated business purpose and revenues come from renting light vehicles. In GICS, vehicle rental belongs to Passenger Ground Transportation, the same sub-industry used for its peers Localiza and Movida.
Quality Software S.A. is a Rio de Janeiro IT services firm that does outsourced IT projects (IT outsourcing and systems development for clients), which fits IT Consulting & Other Services.

company_name: CVC BRASIL OPERADORA E AGÊNCIA DE VIAGENS SA
rationale: CVC Corp (CVCB3) is Brazil's largest tour operator and travel agency group, selling packages, air tickets and hotel stays through stores, franchises and online channels; GICS explicitly places travel agencies and tour operators in Hotels, Resorts & Cruise Lines.

Single-asset generator that owns and runs UTE Pernambuco III, a ~200.8 MW fuel-oil thermal power plant in Igarassu/PE (Bolognesi group) and sells capacity under regulated contracts. Non-renewable power generation makes it an Independent Power Producer.

FTL holds the ANTT concession for public rail freight transport on the original Malha Nordeste network (Malha I), which was split off from Transnordestina Logística S.A. in 2013, and it runs the freight trains itself, so it fits Rail Transportation rather than Highways & Railtracks, which covers owners of track who do not run the trains.

company_name: AXIA ENERGIA UHE SANTO ANTÔNIO S.A.
rationale: Formerly Santo Antônio Energia S.A. and now controlled by Eletrobras/AXIA, the company is a single-asset concession that owns and runs the Santo Antônio hydroelectric plant on the Madeira River in Porto Velho, Rondônia, and sells the power it generates, which makes it a renewable electricity producer.

Aegea is a holding that controls water supply and sewage concessions (e.g., Águas do Rio, Prolagos, Corsan) across Brazilian municipalities, so its dominant revenue comes from water and sanitation services, which places it in Water Utilities.

Serena Geração (formerly Omega Geração S.A.), a subsidiary of Serena Energia, is a holding company. It controls wind, solar and small hydro generation assets in Brazil and sells their electricity, so it fits Renewable Electricity.
Águas Guariroba is the Aegea-controlled concessionaire providing public water supply and sewage services in Campo Grande (MS), a single-concession water/sanitation utility fitting Water Utilities.

company_name: PROLAGOS S/A - CONC.DE SERVICOS PÚBLICOS DE ÁGUA E ESGOTO
rationale: Prolagos, an Aegea Saneamento subsidiary, holds the public concession for water treatment and distribution and sewage collection and treatment in five Região dos Lagos (RJ) municipalities, which makes it a water utility.

Ourofino S.A. (formerly Ouro Fino Saúde Animal Participações, OFSA3) is a holding company. Its operating subsidiaries develop, make and sell veterinary drugs and vaccines for farm and companion animals. GICS puts veterinary drugs under Pharmaceuticals, so the CVM label 'Comércio' does not fit.

company_name: CONC. DO AEROPORTO INTERNACIONAL DE GUARULHOS S.A.
rationale: Single-asset concessionaire that manages, operates, expands and commercially exploits São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport (GRU Airport) under a concession running until 2032, so it fits Airport Services.

Porto Sudeste V.M. is a wholly owned financing vehicle of the iron-ore port company Porto Sudeste do Brasil: it holds 0.43% of the PORT11 royalty securities, issued the matching PSVM11 royalty-based securities to MMX, and has no port operations of its own, so it is classified in Financials as Specialized Finance. Second independent pass proposed 20305030 (Marine Ports & Services).

This América Movil holding company controls Claro S.A. and consolidated about R$42.7bn of revenue in 2022 from integrated telecom services: mobile, fixed-line, broadband and pay-TV. GICS classifies a holding by its single dominant business, so it falls in Integrated Telecommunication Services.

Leads Cia. Securitizadora appears to be a non-bank vehicle that buys credit receivables. Consumer complaints about undue charges and difficulty reaching settlements suggest it buys consumer debt portfolios and collects from debtors, which GICS places in Consumer Finance; this is inferred from secondary sources, not confirmed by primary filings. Second independent pass proposed 40201040 (Specialized Finance).

IMC (B3: MEAL3) runs food-service restaurant chains in Brazil and the US, including Frango Assado, Viena, KFC and Pizza Hut franchises, Margaritaville and catering, so it fits Restaurants rather than the CVM label 'Alimentos'.

Single-asset toll road concessionaire (EcoRodovias group, now branded Ecovias Capixaba) operating and maintaining ~476 km of federal highway BR-101 in Espírito Santo/Bahia under an ANTT concession, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: WIZ CO PARTICIPAÇÕES E CORRETAGEM DE SEGUROS S.A.
rationale: Wiz Co (WIZC3) is a holding whose main business is selling insurance through bancassurance and partner channels, earning brokerage commissions. Most of its revenue and EBITDA come from that insurance distribution, ahead of its smaller credit and consortium distribution units, so it fits Insurance Brokers.

company_name: YOU INC INCORPORADORA E PARTICIPAÇÃO S.A
rationale: You,inc is a São Paulo residential incorporadora that develops, builds and sells residential apartment projects (e.g., the 2025 launch of QG Ferreira de Araujo, R$153m PSV), which fits Homebuilding, the sub-industry used for Brazilian residential incorporadoras such as Cyrela and MRV.

Maestro (Maestro Terceirização de Frotas) earns its revenue from renting light vehicles without drivers and outsourcing corporate fleets (main CNAE: car rental without driver), and GICS puts vehicle rental under Passenger Ground Transportation, the same place as peers like Localiza and Movida.

CBO Holding (Oceana Offshore) controls Grupo CBO, a fleet operator of about 32 offshore support vessels (PSV/AHTS) chartered mainly to oil & gas E&P operators in Brazilian basins and the North Sea; offshore support vessel operators (e.g., Tidewater) fall under Oil & Gas Equipment & Services rather than Marine Transportation.

company_name: LINHAS DE XINGU TRANSMISSORA DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: LXTE is an operating single-asset concession for public electricity transmission (about 508 km of transmission lines in Pará, granted by ANEEL). Under GICS, electricity transmission companies fall under Electric Utilities.

company_name: LINHAS DE MACAPÁ TRANSMISSORA DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Single-asset ANEEL concessionaire (Contract 009/2008, Lot B, Oriximiná–Macapá line) that builds, operates and maintains electricity transmission facilities; transmission companies are classified as Electric Utilities.

Caixa Seguridade is a holding company for Caixa's bancassurance business. Its earnings come from stakes in insurers spread across several lines: life, pension and credit life (Caixa Vida e Previdência/XS1), mortgage and home insurance (CNP/Caixa Residencial), capitalization, consortium and assistance, plus its own brokerage revenue, so Multi-line Insurance fits best.

BRQ Digital Solutions' 2024 Formulário de Referência describes it as a provider of technology and digital transformation services (custom solutions, end-to-end IT services for large corporations), fitting IT Consulting & Other Services.

Movida (a Simpar subsidiary) is Brazil's second-largest car rental (RAC) and fleet outsourcing (GTF) company; used-car sales (~51% of 2024 net revenue) are fleet disposals that are part of the rental model, while earnings and market perception come from vehicle rental, so it fits Passenger Ground Transportation (vehicle rental).

CCR MSVia (Motiva/CCR subsidiary) holds the toll-road concession to operate, maintain and expand 845 km of BR-163/MS from Mundo Novo to Sonora under ANTT, so it is a single-asset toll road operator (Highways & Railtracks).

company_name: CONCEBRA - CONCESSIONARIA DAS RODOVIAS CENTRAIS DO BRASIL S.A.
rationale: Concebra (Triunfo group) holds the federal toll-road concession for BR-060/153/262 (DF/GO/MG). It earns toll revenue from operating these highways, so it fits Highways & Railtracks. Some stretches have already been handed over under the relicitation process, but it still operates the remaining stretches.

Eco050 (now Ecovias Minas Goiás, an EcoRodovias company) holds and operates the 30-year federal toll-road concession for 436.6 km of BR-050 between Delta (MG) and Cristalina (GO), so it is a single-asset toll-road operator, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

This single-asset toll-road concession has run about 851 km of federal highway BR-163 in Mato Grosso since 2014, now as Nova Rota do Oeste. Its revenue comes from tolls, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: CTC - CENTRO DE TECNOLOGIA CANAVIEIRA S.A.
rationale: CTC develops conventional and genetically modified sugarcane varieties (crop genetics/seed technology) and earns nearly all revenue from royalties paid by sugar/ethanol mills for licensed varieties, which best fits agricultural products & services (seed/crop input provider) rather than health-care Biotechnology or ag chemicals.

Alliança Saúde (formerly Alliar / Centro de Imagem Diagnósticos, AALR3) operates diagnostic medicine services, mainly diagnostic imaging and clinical lab testing, including public-private partnerships (PPPs), so it fits Health Care Services, which covers lab testing and diagnostic services.

Travessia is an operating securitization company that issues CRIs (real estate) and CRAs (agribusiness) backed by a mix of receivables, as shown in the trustee reports on B3's Fundos.NET; because the issues span several asset classes rather than being mainly mortgages, Specialized Finance fits better than Mortgage REITs.

Single-asset concessionaire (AB Nascentes das Gerais) operating and maintaining the MG-050 highway corridor under a state concession, earning revenue from toll plazas, which fits Highways & Railtracks.
Azul S.A. is the holding company of Azul Linhas Aéreas Brasileiras. Passenger revenue was about R$14.6bn of R$15.9bn total operating revenue in 2022 (around 92%), so it fits Passenger Airlines.

company_name: ARGO ENERGIA EMPREENDIMENTOS E PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A.
rationale: Holding company that wholly controls Argo I-IV transmission concessionaires (plus 62.5% of Argeb), all dedicated to electric power transmission, which GICS places in Electric Utilities.

Ecoponte (now Ecovias Ponte) is an EcoRodovias concessionaire that holds a federal concession running from 2015 for 30 years to operate the toll-collecting Ponte Rio-Niterói (BR-101/RJ) and its access roads. As a single-asset road and bridge concession, it fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: Companhia Securitizadora de Créditos Financeiros Cartões Consignados I
rationale: A single-purpose securitization company that buys payroll-deducted (consignado) credit card receivables, apparently from Banco BMG's card business, and funds them with debentures; its income is interest on a consumer credit portfolio, so it fits Consumer Finance.

Companhia Energética Sinop is a special-purpose company that holds the concession for and runs the Sinop hydroelectric plant (UHE Sinop, about 400 MW) on the Teles Pires River in Mato Grosso; its owners are EDF, Chesf and Eletronorte, and the plant has run commercially since 2019, so as a single-asset hydropower generator it fits Renewable Electricity.
IRB-Brasil Resseguros (IRB(Re), B3: IRBR3) is Brazil's largest reinsurer, getting most of its revenue from reinsurance premiums written for ceding insurers, which fits the Reinsurance sub-industry.

Argo Transmissão de Energia (Argo I) is a single-asset company holding a 30-year ANEEL public-service concession (Auction 013/2015, Lot A) to build, operate and maintain the 500 kV Bacabeira–Pecém II transmission line of about 1,150 km and its substations; GICS puts electricity transmission in Electric Utilities.

Camil processes, packages and sells branded food products such as rice, beans, sugar (União), canned fish (Coqueiro), pasta and coffee in Brazil and other Latin American countries, which makes it a branded packaged-foods producer.

Priner's main business is industrial maintenance services for oil & gas, mining, pulp & paper, steel and petrochemical plants: assembling and renting access scaffolding (about 45% of revenue), industrial painting, surface treatment and thermal insulation. GICS names industrial maintenance services under Diversified Support Services, so that fits better than the CVM construction label.

company_name: SMARTFIT ESCOLA DE GINÁSTICA E DANÇA S.A.
rationale: Smart Fit (SMFT3) runs Latin America's largest chain of high-value, low-price gyms, and most of its revenue comes from gym memberships, which fits Leisure Facilities (operators of sport and fitness centers).

INC Empreendimentos Imobiliários (formerly Inter Construtora e Incorporadora, Juiz de Fora) designs, develops, builds and sells residential units, mainly affordable housing, so it fits Homebuilding like its Brazilian peers such as MRV and Tenda.

Vibra Energia (formerly BR Distribuidora) is Brazil's largest fuel distributor. Nearly all of its roughly R$168bn in revenue comes from marketing fuels and lubricants, through the BR service-station network (61% of revenue) and B2B sales including aviation fuel (39%), which fits Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing; renewables are a small share.

ZAMP S.A. (formerly BK Brasil Operação e Assessoria a Restaurantes) owns and operates Burger King, Popeyes, Subway and Starbucks restaurants in Brazil, which puts it in Restaurants rather than the CVM's 'Alimentos' label.
Entrevias holds a toll-road concession from ARTESP, signed in June 2017, to run highways in central-western São Paulo state, so as a single-asset road concession it belongs in Highways & Railtracks.

Hapvida is a holding company whose dominant business, through Hapvida and NotreDame Intermédica, is running health and dental plans. Its own hospitals and clinics support those plans, and most revenue comes from risk-based plan premiums, so it fits Managed Health Care.

Single-asset concession SPE controlled by ENGIE Brasil Energia that holds the 30-year concession and operates the 424 MW Jaguara hydroelectric plant (UHE Jaguara), so it is a hydropower generator and falls under Renewable Electricity.

Engie Brasil's single-asset concession company (CVM code 2443-0) whose principal activity is generating electricity by operating the Miranda hydroelectric plant (UHE Miranda), so it fits Renewable Electricity (hydropower).

Belém Transmissora is a single-asset electricity transmission concession company whose revenues come from transmission infrastructure (contract-asset remuneration and implementation revenue), and electricity transmission is classified under Electric Utilities.

Tapajós Transmissora (CNPJ 27.967.244/0001-02) holds ANEEL transmission concession(s), including contract 048/2017 in Pará through 2047 from ANEEL Auction 05/2016, and builds, operates and maintains transmission facilities, which places it in Electric Utilities because GICS puts electricity transmission there.

Prática (Pouso Alegre, MG) manufactures professional foodservice equipment (combination/speed ovens, bakery machinery, proofers, blast chillers under Technicook/Tecnipan/Klimaquip brands), commercial kitchen machinery that GICS places in Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components (peer precedent: Middleby, Welbilt).

This holding is controlled by Energisa S/A and owns 100% of the group's electricity transmission concessionaires (Energisa Goiás, Pará II, Tocantins, Amazonas Transmissoras, etc.), and GICS puts electricity transmission in Electric Utilities.

company_name: CELEO REDES TRANSMISSÃO DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Celeo Redes Transmissão de Energia is a holding company within the Celeo Redes Brasil group whose subsidiaries hold ANEEL electricity transmission line concessions, such as LT Triângulo, which it has absorbed by merger; electricity transmission falls under Electric Utilities.

Banco BMG is a multiple bank, but most of its business is consumer credit. Its retail loan book centres on payroll-deductible credit cards (its main product, per its results releases), payroll loans and personal credit for INSS retirees and public servants. That fits Consumer Finance better than Regional Banks, although its deposit funding and a smaller corporate lending segment make Regional Banks a reasonable alternative. Second independent pass proposed 40101015 (Regional Banks).

Blau Farmacêutica (BLAU3) develops, manufactures and sells prescription drugs, mostly hospital injectables. Its products include biologics, plasma-derived drugs, oncology drugs, antibiotics and anesthetics, made at its own plants in Brazil and sold across Latin America and the US, which makes it a diversified drug maker that fits Pharmaceuticals rather than a pure biotech.

BBM Logística (BBML3) is one of the largest road-freight logistics operators in Brazil and Mercosur. It earns its revenue from road transport and dedicated truck-fleet operations, which fits Cargo Ground Transportation.

Grupo SBF is a holding company for Centauro, Brazil's largest sporting-goods retail chain, and Fisia, Nike's official operator in Brazil, which runs Nike's own stores and e-commerce and also sells wholesale; most consolidated revenue comes from sporting-goods retail, which GICS places in Other Specialty Retail (the same place as peers like Dick's), even though Fisia's wholesale business is a significant mixed segment.

company_name: NOVA TRANSPORTADORA DO SUDESTE S.A. - NTS
rationale: NTS runs ANP-regulated high-pressure natural gas transmission pipelines in Southeast Brazil (RJ/SP/MG). It earns capacity-contract revenue from shippers rather than distributing gas to end users, so it fits midstream Oil & Gas Storage & Transportation.

company_name: VAMOS LOCAÇÃO DE CAMINHÕES, MÁQUINAS E EQUIPAMENTOS S.A.
rationale: Vamos makes most of its revenue from long-term rental of trucks, machinery and equipment to businesses, plus resale of used assets; GICS places lessors of transportation equipment and rental of industrial machinery to businesses in Trading Companies & Distributors.

Copel GeT is Copel's wholly owned generation and transmission subsidiary. Most of its revenue comes from hydroelectric and wind generation, with power transmission concessions as a smaller second segment, so it fits Renewable Electricity.

unclassified_reason: Litela was only a vehicle for holding Vale S.A. shares for Previ/BB Carteira Ativa. It handed those Vale shares to its shareholders through capital reductions in 2019–2020, and shareholders approved its dissolution in December 2020. It is now in liquidation with no operating activity, so no sub-industry applies.
rationale: This was a single-asset holding of Vale shares (which would have pointed to Steel/iron ore), but it has distributed those shares and has been in liquidation since its December 2020 dissolution, so it has no current business to classify.

Vivara Participações is the holding of Brazil's largest jewelry chain (Vivara and Life brands), which earns most of its revenue by selling jewelry, watches and accessories through its own stores and e-commerce, so it fits Other Specialty Retail, where jewelry retailers are listed by name; it also makes about 80% of what it sells at its own Manaus factory, which leaves some overlap with Apparel, Accessories & Luxury Goods.

Localiza Fleet is a wholly owned subsidiary of Localiza Rent a Car that runs its fleet-management business, renting cars to companies on long-term contracts, and it also sells the cars it takes out of service; vehicle rental falls under Passenger Ground Transportation, the same sub-industry as its parent.

Rede D'Or is Brazil's largest private hospital operator. It ran 78 hospitals at end-2024, and its hospital segment brought in about R$28bn in net revenue, the largest share of revenue and earnings. That fits Health Care Facilities, although the SulAmérica health-insurance segment it took over in 2022 is a large second business (hence medium confidence).

BRK Ambiental Participações is a holding company (formerly Odebrecht Ambiental, controlled by Brookfield) whose dominant business through its SPEs is water supply and sewage collection/treatment concessions and PPPs, so it fits Water Utilities.

C&A Modas runs a national chain of more than 300 own stores plus e-commerce in Brazil. Most of its revenue comes from selling apparel, accessories and some fashiontronics and beauty products in those stores, so it fits Apparel Retail rather than the Textiles label CVM gives it.

company_name: ENERGISA SUL-SUDESTE - DISTRIBUIDORA DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Energisa Sul-Sudeste is an ANEEL-regulated electricity distribution concessionaire (Energisa group) serving ~82 municipalities in western São Paulo, Paraná and Minas Gerais, so electricity distribution to end users fits Electric Utilities.

company_name: LIFEMED INDUSTRIAL DE EQUIP. E ART. MEDICOS E HOSP. S.A.
rationale: Lifemed makes medical devices for hospitals and ICUs at its plant in Pelotas, including infusion pumps, monitors, defibrillators and ventilators, which fits Health Care Equipment (35101010). It also sells the disposable IV sets that go with its pumps and rents out equipment, so part of its revenue is in disposables.

company_name: LM TRANSPORTES INTERESTADUAIS SERVIÇOS E COMÉRCIO S.A.
rationale: LM Transportes Interestaduais (LM Frotas / LM Mobilidade), based in Salvador, earns its revenue mainly from renting and outsourcing vehicle fleets, with CNAE 7711-0/00 (car rental without driver), so it fits the vehicle rental part of Passenger Ground Transportation, the same sub-industry as Brazilian peers Localiza and Movida.

company_name: MITRE REALTY EMPREENDIMENTOS E PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A.
rationale: Mitre Realty (MTRE3) builds and develops residential apartment buildings in São Paulo for sale to homeowners, mainly middle- and high-income buyers. That is the same as its Brazilian incorporadora peers, which are classified as Homebuilding.

LWSA (formerly Locaweb) gets most of its revenue (about 69% in 2Q24, R$230.5M of R$336M) from its Commerce segment, which sells cloud software to businesses: Tray e-commerce platforms, Bling ERP and Vindi payment/subscription tools. A smaller BeOnline/SaaS segment covers hosting, so cloud application software fits best and Internet Services & Infrastructure is secondary.

TIM S.A. is one of Brazil's largest mobile network operators, and it describes mobile as its main line of business, with most of its service revenue coming from mobile (fixed broadband via TIM Ultrafibra is a smaller part), so it fits Wireless Telecommunication Services.

LAMSA is the single-asset concessionaire that operates the tolled Linha Amarela urban expressway in Rio de Janeiro, under a municipal concession that runs to 2037; it was controlled by Invepar and is now controlled by Mubadala, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Single-asset company owning and operating the 345 MW coal-fired Pampa Sul thermoelectric plant in Candiota (RS), selling power under long-term PPAs (formerly ENGIE, now Starboard/Perfin), i.e., a non-renewable independent power producer.

company_name: ALLPARK EMPREENDIMENTOS, PARTICIPAÇÕES E SERVIÇOS S.A.
rationale: Allpark (Estapar, ALPK3) is Brazil's largest parking operator, earning most of its revenue from running leased, managed and concession car parks and on-street rotating-parking contracts, a business-service activity that matches how peer parking operators such as SP Plus are classified under Diversified Support Services.

company_name: NORTE BRASIL TRANSMISSORA DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: This is a single-asset concession company that builds, operates and maintains the 2,411 km ±600 kV HVDC transmission line from Porto Velho (RO) to Araraquara 2 (SP) as part of the national grid's Rede Básica, and GICS puts electricity transmission in Electric Utilities.

SIMPAR (formerly JSL S.A.) is a holding company that runs and controls eight subsidiaries in several GICS sectors, with no single sub-industry making up most of revenue: JSL in road logistics, Movida in car rental, Vamos in truck and equipment rental, CS Brasil in fleet services, CS Infra in concessions, Ciclus in waste management, Automob in car dealerships and BBC in banking. This fits Industrial Conglomerates better than a single sub-industry or Multi-Sector Holdings. Second independent pass proposed 20304040 (Passenger Ground Transportation).

Lojas Quero-Quero runs a chain of more than 500 home and construction stores, mainly in southern Brazil. Most of its revenue comes from retail sales of building materials and home improvement products, which fits Home Improvement Retail. Its credit operations (VerdeCard) support the retail business and are not its main activity.

d1000 Varejo Farma is the Profarma Group's retail unit, a holding company whose only business is running pharmacy chains in Rio de Janeiro and nearby areas (Drogasmil, Farmalife, Drogaria Tamoio, Drogarias Rosário), so it fits Drug Retail.

Lavvi is a São Paulo developer and builder (incorporadora e construtora) of mid- to high-end residential apartments sold to homeowners, with revenue from unit sales, so it fits Homebuilding as its Brazilian residential-developer peers do.

Plano & Plano is a São Paulo developer and builder of affordable residential apartments, mainly under the Minha Casa Minha Vida program. It builds the units itself and sells them to homebuyers, which fits Homebuilding, the same way Brazilian peers such as MRV and Direcional are classified.
Norte Energia is the single-asset concessionaire of the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant (UHE Belo Monte, Pará), generating and selling hydropower, which fits Renewable Electricity.

Cury (CURY3) builds and sells residential apartments, mainly affordable housing under Minha Casa Minha Vida in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, so it fits Homebuilding, in line with peers MRV and Direcional.
Melnick (MELK3) develops, builds and sells mostly high-end residential apartment projects in metropolitan Porto Alegre, matching Homebuilding, as with peers Cyrela, Even and EZTEC.

Compass Gás e Energia (Cosan group) is a holding whose dominant operating business is regulated piped natural gas distribution through Comgás (São Paulo concession) plus other state distributors (Sulgás, Necta etc.), with smaller LNG/marketing activities, fitting Gas Utilities.

Pacaembu Construtora develops, builds and sells low-income residential housing units (mainly single-family houses under the Minha Casa Minha Vida programme) in São Paulo state, which is residential construction for sale to homeowners, consistent with how Brazilian MCMV builders are treated as Homebuilding.

Sequoia (Move3) is an operating Brazilian logistics company. Its core business is e-commerce logistics: parcel and last-mile delivery, fulfillment and integrated logistics, with road freight (Transportadora Americana) on the side. This fits Air Freight & Logistics (courier, logistics and package delivery) better than pure trucking, and the company is still operating under an out-of-court debt restructuring.

company_name: COMPANHIA DE GÁS DE MINAS GERAIS - GASMIG
rationale: Gasmig, controlled by Cemig, holds the state concession as the exclusive distributor of piped natural gas across Minas Gerais, which is a core Gas Utilities activity.

Grupo Mateus is a holding of Brazil's third-largest supermarket chain, with most of its gross revenue from food cash & carry (atacarejo, ~56%) and supermarket/hypermarket retail (~24%), plus a smaller wholesale distribution segment (~17%), making food retail its dominant activity. Second independent pass proposed 30101040 (Consumer Staples Merchandise Retail).

Alares Internet Participações is the holding of the Alares group (formerly Grupo Conexão), a fixed FTTH fiber broadband ISP serving ~500k residential subscribers in six Brazilian states; ISPs providing internet access to end users fall under Integrated Telecommunication Services.

Track&Field (TFCO4) designs and sells its own sportswear brand mostly through its own stores, plus franchised stores (goods sold to franchisees and royalties) and e-commerce; GICS puts apparel makers that sell mainly through their own retail channels in Apparel Retail.

Méliuz makes most of its revenue (record R$460m in 2025) from commissions paid by partner retailers and financial-product partners on its cashback/rewards platform (affiliate performance marketing and reward programs), which fits Advertising; its bitcoin treasury affects profit through mark-to-market gains but brings in no meaningful operating revenue.

company_name: TRAVESSIA SECURITIZADORA DE CRÉDITOS FINANCEIROS S.A.
rationale: Operating securitization vehicle that acquires financial credit receivables and funds them by issuing multi-series debentures backed by fiduciary assignment of those receivables, a specialized financing activity best fitting Specialized Finance.

Enjoei runs online marketplaces (Enjoei for used and new fashion, accessories and lifestyle goods, plus its subsidiary Elo7 for handmade goods) and earns its revenue mainly from transaction commissions and seller services, which fits an online marketplace selling mostly consumer discretionary merchandise, so Broadline Retail.

Alphaville S.A. (AVLL3) is a holding company whose wholly owned subsidiary, Alphaville Urbanismo, develops and sells residential and mixed-use communities, mainly urbanized lots in gated developments, so it fits Real Estate Development rather than Homebuilding or construction.

company_name: AERIS IND. E COM. DE EQUIP. PARA GER. DE ENG. S.A.
rationale: Aeris Energy is Latin America's leading manufacturer of wind turbine blades. Blade manufacturing is the majority of revenue, and blade maintenance and inspection services under Aeris Services make up the remaining ~30%. Turbine components fit Heavy Electrical Equipment, the same treatment as peers like TPI Composites.

Brava Energia (formerly 3R Petroleum, merged with Enauta) is an independent oil and gas producer with onshore assets (Potiguar, Recôncavo) and offshore assets (Atlanta, Papa-Terra, Peroá); upstream production drives the business, and its Potiguar refining/midstream segment is a vertically linked complement rather than a separate integrated-major business, so it fits E&P.

Patrimar is a Belo Horizonte-based construction and development company. It builds and sells residential apartments under its Patrimar brand (high-end) and Novolar brand (economy segment) in MG, RJ and SP, which fits Homebuilding, in line with peer Brazilian construtoras/incorporadoras such as MRV, Cyrela and Direcional.

Allied distributes consumer electronics, mainly smartphones and other tech hardware, wholesale to retailers and carriers in Brazil and abroad. Distribution was about 74% of 2024 net revenue of R$5.5bn, with digital and physical retail making up the rest, so it fits Technology Distributors.

Elfa Medicamentos (Grupo Elfa, controlled by Pátria funds) mainly distributes medicines and medical/surgical supplies to hospitals, clinics and health plans across Brazil, which places it in Health Care Distributors rather than the CVM label "Serviços Médicos".

company_name: CONCESSIONÁRIA DAS RODOVIAS INTEGRADAS DO SUL S.A.
rationale: The company is CCR ViaSul (Motiva group), the single-asset federal toll-road concession operating highways in Rio Grande do Sul (BR-101/290/386/448), so it is classified as an owner/operator of roads.

Sendas Distribuidora runs Assaí Atacadista, a nationwide chain of cash-and-carry warehouse stores in Brazil that sell food, household and personal care products in bulk to small businesses and end consumers, which fits a hypermarket/warehouse-club staples retailer (Consumer Staples Merchandise Retail) rather than a pure food retailer or B2B distributor.

EZ INC is the commercial real estate subsidiary of EZTEC. It develops high-end corporate office towers, has plans for logistics warehouses, and also earns some lease income, so its principal activity best fits Real Estate Development rather than Homebuilding or an operating/leasing company.

HBR Realty develops, owns, leases and manages its own portfolio of income-producing commercial properties: ComVem convenience centers, HBR 3A high-end corporate offices, HBR Malls shopping centers and other assets. Most of its revenue is rental income, which fits Real Estate Operating Companies (it is a corporation, not a REIT), not the coarse CVM construction label.

company_name: SBF COMÉRCIO DE PRODUTOS ESPORTIVOS S.A.
rationale: SBF Comércio de Produtos Esportivos is the Grupo SBF operating company behind Centauro, Latin America's largest sporting goods retail chain, and sporting goods retail falls under Other Specialty Retail (same as peers such as Dick's and Academy Sports).
Farmácia e Drogaria Nissei (NISS3) runs Farmácias Nissei, a retail pharmacy/drugstore chain with 470+ stores in PR, SC, SP, GO and DF, so most of its revenue comes from drug retail.

Urba is MRV&CO's urban development arm. It develops planned residential and commercial land subdivisions (loteamentos) and sells the lots, which makes it a real estate developer rather than a homebuilder or a construction contractor.

MPM Corpóreos (B3: ESPA) owns the Espaçolaser chain of own and franchised laser hair-removal/aesthetic clinics, a consumer personal care service, which fits Specialized Consumer Services rather than health care facilities despite the CVM 'Serviços Médicos' label.

company_name: INTELBRAS S.A. IND. DE TELECOMUNICAÇÃO ELETRÔNICA BRASILEIRA
rationale: Intelbras designs and manufactures electronic equipment (plants in Santa Catarina and Manaus); its largest segment, Security (CCTV cameras, recorders, alarms, access control and intercoms, about 54-56% of net revenue in 2024), is security system equipment, which GICS puts in Electronic Equipment & Instruments, with ICT/networking and solar energy equipment as smaller segments; the CVM label "Comércio" is outdated.

company_name: GRUPO TOKY S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Grupo Toky (formerly Mobly S.A.) owns the Tok&Stok and Mobly brands. It sells furniture and home furnishings to consumers through online and physical stores, which fits Homefurnishing Retail. The stores are still operating during the judicial recovery.

Jalles Machado grows and processes sugarcane in Goiás into sugar (conventional and organic), ethanol and bioelectricity; revenue is split between sugar and ethanol (ethanol made up about 50–60% of the 2026/27 production mix), and in line with Brazilian sugar-mill peers and market perception as an agribusiness cane processor, it fits Agricultural Products & Services rather than Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing.

Bemobi has moved from mobile app subscriptions to recurring digital payment processing for utilities, telecoms and other essential-service billers (Bemobi Pay, Paytime). Payments are now its largest revenue line, about 52% of net revenue in 3Q26, and the market sees it as a payments company; SaaS and subscription revenue make up the rest.

Westwing (B3: WEST3) is a Brazilian online retailer focused on home & living products (furniture, decor, housewares) that it sells to consumers as a merchant, which fits Homefurnishing Retail rather than Broadline Retail.

Cruzeiro do Sul Educacional (B3: CSED3) is a private higher-education group in Brazil running universities and university centers with on-campus and digital/distance-learning undergraduate and graduate programs, so tuition is its main revenue and it fits Education Services.

OceanPact earns most revenue from chartering offshore support vessels (OSRV, PSV, RSV), mainly to Petrobras and other offshore oil & gas operators, plus subsea, logistics and engineering services, which fits Oil & Gas Equipment & Services; its oil-spill response business makes Environmental & Facilities Services a possible alternative.

company_name: CVLB BRASIL S.A EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICAL
rationale: CVLB Brasil (formerly Lojas Le Biscuit S.A.) was formed in 2023 by merging Casa&Video and Le Biscuit. It is still trading during judicial recovery, running about 307 discount stores in 14 states that sell a broad mix of housewares, small appliances and electronics, home décor, toys and gifts, so it fits Broadline Retail (general/discount merchandise) better than any single specialty-retail category.

Orizon operates waste-treatment ecoparks (sanitary landfills) whose core revenue is waste disposal fees, supplemented by biogas, energy, recycling and carbon credits, fitting waste management under Environmental & Facilities Services rather than the coarse CVM sanitation label.

company_name: EQUATORIAL GOIAS DISTRIBUIDORA DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Equatorial Goiás (formerly CELG D) is the regulated electricity distribution concessionaire for 237 municipalities in Goiás state (CNAE 3514-0/00, distribution of electric energy), which fits Electric Utilities.
CSN Mineração is the iron-ore mining arm of CSN, operating the Casa de Pedra complex in Congonhas (MG), and iron ore sales are its main source of revenue; GICS puts iron ore mining under Steel.

ViaPaulista S.A. is an Arteris toll-road concessionaire operating about 720 km of São Paulo state highways (Ribeirão Preto, Franca, Araraquara and Botucatu regions) under a 30-year concession, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: ÁGUAS DE TERESINA SANEAMENTO SPE S.A.
rationale: Aegea-controlled SPE holding the sub-concession (from AGESPISA, through 2047) for public water supply and sewage collection/treatment in urban Teresina (PI), a regulated water utility activity.

Rio Paraná Energia (CTG Brasil subsidiary) holds the 30-year ANEEL concession to operate the Jupiá and Ilha Solteira hydroelectric plants (~5 GW), so its revenue comes from hydropower generation, i.e., Renewable Electricity.

Kalunga sells stationery, school and office supplies, and IT products and printers through more than 120 stores of its own, an online store and telesales. Office-supplies retailers like this fit GICS Other Specialty Retail, though IT products are a significant share of sales.

Auren Participações S.A. (formerly AES Brasil Energia S.A., same CNPJ, acquired by Auren Energia in 2024) is a holding company whose dominant operating business is renewable power generation from hydro, wind and solar assets, plus related energy trading, which fits Renewable Electricity.

company_name: AGROGALAXY PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: AgroGalaxy is a holding company whose dominant business is a network of stores reselling agricultural inputs to farmers (crop-protection chemicals, fertilizers and seeds), with grain trading on the side. It is still operating under judicial recovery. B2B distribution of agrochemicals and fertilizers fits Trading Companies & Distributors.

HMOBI is a Mubadala-controlled holding whose main operating business is MetrôRio (Concessão Metroviária do Rio de Janeiro, together with Metrô Barra/Line 4), which earns its revenue from passenger subway fares, so it fits Rail Transportation; the recent Lamsa toll-road stake is a smaller part of the business.

CM Hospitalar S.A. (Viveo) gets most of its revenue from distributing medicines and medical/hospital products to hospitals, clinics, laboratories and pharmacies, with manufacturing (Cremer) as a minority segment, so it fits Health Care Distributors.

Hospital Mater Dei S.A. (B3: MATD3) owns and runs the Rede Mater Dei de Saúde private hospital network, centered in Belo Horizonte, and most of its revenue comes from hospital services, which fits Health Care Facilities.

Boa Safra (SOJA3) produces and sells seed, mainly soybean seed (about R$889m of R$1,089m gross revenue in 3Q26), plus newer seed crops; growing crops as an agricultural product fits Agricultural Products & Services better than Fertilizers & Agricultural Chemicals.

GPS Participações (Grupo GPS, GGPS3) is a holding company whose operating subsidiaries provide outsourced services that rely heavily on labor. Most of its business is integrated facilities services such as cleaning, reception, landscaping and building maintenance; it also provides security, industrial maintenance and indoor logistics. Facilities management fits Environmental & Facilities Services best, but Diversified Support Services is a close alternative. Second independent pass proposed 20201070 (Diversified Support Services).

company_name: RIO ALTO ENERGIAS RENOVÁVEIS S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Rio Alto develops and operates solar photovoltaic plants in Paraíba (Coremas, Santa Luzia complexes) and sells the electricity they generate, which makes it a renewable electricity producer; confidence is medium because of its restructuring and the December 2025 loss of control of the Coremas complex.

Infracommerce is a white-label "Customer Experience as a Service" provider that runs end-to-end digital commerce operations for brands (platform, data, logistics, payments, customer service) and earns mainly service fees, which makes it a business-process-outsourcing provider rather than a retailer, despite the CVM's commerce label.

Vittia (VITT3) makes and sells specialty fertilizers (foliar fertilizers, micronutrients, soil conditioners) and biological crop protection products and inoculants, all agricultural chemicals, so it fits Fertilizers & Agricultural Chemicals rather than the coarse CVM sugar/ethanol agriculture label.

Campinas-based holding that owns and operates a network of about 11 hospitals (1,206 beds) and clinics across SP, SC and PR; its two small health plans (around 102k lives) are secondary, so hospital operation is the dominant activity, which fits Health Care Facilities.

PetroReconcavo is an independent onshore oil and natural gas producer working mature fields in Bahia and the Potiguar Basin; it has no significant refining or chemicals business, so it fits Oil & Gas Exploration & Production.

Kallas (Grupo Kallas) builds and develops mid- to high-end residential apartments for sale in São Paulo state and funds this with debentures and CRIs; this matches Homebuilding, the sub-industry used for Brazilian residential construtoras/incorporadoras such as Cyrela, MRV and Even.

Rodobens S.A. is a non-financial holding (CNAE 64620) whose consolidated revenue appears to come mainly from its automotive retail segment (Toyota car and Mercedes-Benz truck dealerships, 24.9k units sold in 2024), with consórcio, Banco Rodobens and insurance as important but smaller-revenue financial segments, so Automotive Retail fits by principal revenue source.

Dotz runs a coalition loyalty program in Brazil, which made up about 58% of revenue in 2024. GICS places reward program management in Advertising, but the fast-growing techfin business (37% in 2024, near half by 1Q25) could change the dominant activity.

Tegra Incorporadora (formerly Brookfield Incorporações, part of the Brookfield group) mainly develops, builds and sells mid- to high-end residential apartments in São Paulo, Campinas and Rio de Janeiro, so it fits Homebuilding, the sub-industry where Brazilian residential incorporadoras such as Cyrela and MRV are classified.

W2W (Wine.com.br) is a wine importer and direct-to-consumer retailer that sells mainly through its e-commerce site, a wine subscription club and its own stores; wine is a consumer-staples beverage, so the closest fit is Food Retail (specialty beverage/liquor retail), although wholesale/B2B import sales make the mix less clear-cut.

BR Partners is a Brazilian independent investment bank (holding of Banco BR Partners) whose largest revenue line is Investment Banking + Capital Markets (M&A advisory, DCM/ECM), complemented by treasury sales & structuring and wealth management, fitting Investment Banking & Brokerage.

Kora Saúde is a holding company whose main business is a network of private hospitals (Espírito Santo, Ceará through Grupo OTO, and other states), and most of its revenue comes from hospital services, so it fits Health Care Facilities.

The former GetNinjas, renamed REAG Investimentos and then Arandu Investimentos, is now a holding focused on asset and wealth management (B3 profile), and its 2025 revenue came mostly from consolidated asset managers and funds rather than the legacy GetNinjas services marketplace, so it fits Asset Management & Custody Banks. Second independent pass proposed 50203010 (Interactive Media & Services).

company_name: LIVETECH DA BAHIA INDÚSTRIA E COMÉRCIO S.A.
rationale: Livetech da Bahia (WDC Networks, WDCN3) mainly sells and leases (Technology as a Service) telecom, IT and solar equipment from third-party vendors to ISPs, operators and businesses, with Telecom as the largest segment, so it fits Technology Distributors better than a manufacturer or telecom carrier.

Emccamp is a Belo Horizonte-based incorporadora and construtora that develops and builds low-income residential housing (Minha Casa Minha Vida / Casa Verde e Amarela) in MG, SP and RJ for sale to homeowners, consistent with how Brazilian residential builder-developers like MRV are classified in Homebuilding.

Raízen S.A. (Cosan/Shell JV) gets most of its revenue from marketing Shell-branded fuels and lubricants in Brazil and Argentina, where it also runs a refinery, and it produces ethanol; under the approved out-of-court restructuring plan, fuel distribution stays with Raízen S.A., which fits Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing.

Bionexo runs a SaaS and e-procurement platform for hospitals and clinics, covering hospital supply purchasing, inventory and revenue-cycle tools, and it bought Philips' Tasy hospital-management/EHR software. Because it provides IT mainly to health care providers, it fits Health Care Technology better than the coarse CVM label "Comunicação e Informática".

3tentos is an integrated agribusiness: it sells farm inputs (retail), originates and trades grain (soybean, corn, wheat), and crushes soybeans into meal, oil and biodiesel; most of its revenue comes from grain trading and crushing, which places it with agricultural processors and merchants like ADM and Bunge in Agricultural Products & Services.

CBA (CBAV3) is a vertically integrated aluminum producer, mining bauxite and making primary aluminum and rolled/extruded products, with some aluminum recycling, so it fits Aluminum rather than the CVM label of mineral extraction.

Terra Santa Propriedades Agrícolas is a rural real estate company that owns seven farms in Mato Grosso and earns most of its revenue by leasing them, mainly to SLC Agrícola on long-term leases; because it is a non-REIT landlord rather than a crop producer, it fits Real Estate Operating Companies.

Desktop S.A. (DESK3) is a São Paulo-based fiber-optic broadband internet service provider selling internet access to end users (over 1 million clients), which falls under Integrated Telecommunication Services. Claro is acquiring a controlling stake, but Desktop is still operating.

Grupo Multi (Multilaser) designs, makes and sells branded consumer tech hardware: smartphones, tablets, notebooks, computer peripherals and IT supplies. In 2024 these made up about half of revenue (Office & IT Supplies R$1.05B plus Mobile Devices R$0.68B, out of R$3.39B), ahead of home appliances, kids/sports and health, which fits Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals; B3 also lists it under Computers & Equipment.

Unifique is a southern-Brazil fiber-optic ISP. Most of its revenue comes from fixed broadband, with smaller fixed telephony and mobile lines, which fits Integrated Telecommunication Services (ISPs serving end users, fixed plus wireless).

company_name: ARMAC LOCAÇÃO, LOGÍSTICA E SERVIÇOS S.A.
rationale: Armac's main business is renting heavy machinery to businesses, mainly yellow-line equipment and trucks (~90% of revenue); GICS puts industrial machinery rental to other businesses in Trading Companies & Distributors.

Economatica S.A. (formerly TC S.A./Traders Club, renamed in 2026; ticker ECOM3) runs the Economatica financial data and analytics platform. Its clients are investment banks, pension funds, brokers and asset managers, so it fits Financial Exchanges & Data as a provider of financial decision-support tools. Confidence is medium because the legacy retail-investor community and content business has not been measured against the data business by revenue.

company_name: CIA SECURITIZADORA DE CRED. FIN. CARTÕES CONSIGNADOS II
rationale: Banco BMG-controlled securitization vehicle that acquires payroll-deductible (consignado) credit card receivables and funds them through debentures (CRCG11/CRCG22), earning yield on a consumer credit card portfolio, so its economic activity is consumer finance.

company_name: ONCOCLÍNICAS DO BRASIL SERVIÇOS MÉDICOS S.A.
rationale: Oncoclínicas owns and operates a national network of outpatient oncology clinics integrated with high-complexity Cancer Centers/hospitals, deriving most revenue from patient treatment at its own facilities, which fits Health Care Facilities (vs. Health Care Services as an alternative for the infusion-clinic component).

The name points to small hydroelectric plants ("PCHs", pequenas centrais hidrelétricas). The company appears to be the former Brasil PCH S.A., now held by Pátria's Essentia Energia, which generates and sells hydropower from its PCH portfolio, so it fits Renewable Electricity.

The legal name ("Hortifrut", meaning fresh fruit and vegetables) and the CVM label (Comércio – Atacado e Varejo) point to fresh-produce trading, most likely a hortifruti store chain, which fits Food Retail; web search failed, so no primary source confirms this or rules out wholesale distribution (30101020).

Auren Operações (formerly AES Tietê / AES Brasil Operações, CNPJ 00.194.724/0001-13, CNAE 3511-5/01 electricity generation) is now part of the Auren Energia group and owns and operates hydro, wind and solar generation assets, so it fits Renewable Electricity.
Teuto is a Brazilian pharmaceutical manufacturer based in Anápolis (GO), and its main products are generic, branded and OTC drugs, plus some biosimilars, so it fits Pharmaceuticals.

Caramuru is a soybean and corn originator and processor (soy meal, oil, protein concentrates, corn derivatives) with most of its revenue from commodity and differentiated-commodity agri-processing; biofuels (31% of 2025 revenue) and consumer products are minority segments, so it fits Agricultural Products & Services, similar to Bunge and ADM.

company_name: BLUEFIT ACADEMIAS DE GINÁSTICA E PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A
rationale: Bluefit owns and runs a chain of fitness centers in Brazil, which matches GICS Leisure Facilities (owners and operators of sport and fitness centers).

Tigre S.A. Participações is the holding company of Grupo Tigre, whose main business is making PVC pipes, fittings and related plumbing and building components for construction in Brazil, Latin America and the US (consolidated net revenue of about R$1.34bn in 3Q25), so it belongs in Building Products.

Comerc Energia is a holding company. Its subsidiaries generate renewable power, mainly centralized solar, solar distributed generation and wind, with about 2.2 GW installed. They also trade and manage power contracts in Brazil's free energy market. Renewable generation drives most of the EBITDA (R$1.08bn in 2024, attributed to new solar plants and growth in distributed generation), so the company fits Renewable Electricity rather than IPP/Energy Traders. Second independent pass proposed 55105010 (Independent Power Producers & Energy Traders).

Austravias (formerly Monte Rodovias) is a holding company whose dominant business is operating toll-road concessions (Rota dos Coqueiros, Rota do Atlântico, Bahia Norte, Litoral Norte, Rota Dourada), so it is classified as an owner/operator of roads.

Rodovias do Brasil Holding is a mono-holding that controls Concessionária Rota das Bandeiras (CRB), which runs the Corredor Dom Pedro toll-road concession around Campinas and Jundiaí in São Paulo, so it is classified as a toll-road owner and operator.

Madero runs restaurant chains in Brazil (Madero Steak House, Madero Container, Jeronimo), and its registered CNAE is restaurants. Its central kitchen mainly supplies its own outlets, so restaurant sales are the dominant revenue, and Restaurants fits better than the CVM 'Alimentos' label.

Almeida Junior owns and operates a portfolio of shopping centers in Santa Catarina (Garten, Neumarkt, Norte, Continente, Balneário Camboriú, Nações), earning mainly rental and mall management income; as a non-REIT mall owner and operator, like Multiplan and Iguatemi, it fits Real Estate Operating Companies.

Vero S.A. (Vero Internet) is a fixed-line fiber broadband ISP whose main registered activity is multimedia communication services (SCM), providing internet access to end users, which fits Integrated Telecommunication Services.

Aço Verde do Brasil (AVB) runs an integrated long-steel mill in Açailândia, Maranhão, that makes its steel with charcoal-based pig iron, so iron and steel production is its main activity and it fits the Steel sub-industry.

unclassified_reason: The company is a Brazilian SPAC (special purpose acquisition company), sponsored by Alvarez & Marsal Holdings LLC. Its CVM status is FASE PRÉ-OPERACIONAL, and I found no evidence that it completed a business combination or has any operating business. It is a pre-operational shell, so no sub-industry applies.
rationale: The company's own Fato Relevante (Dec 2021) calls it a SPAC that received CVM Category A registration and is managed by the sponsor Alvarez & Marsal Holdings LLC; its CNAE is non-financial holding, and it has no operating activity.

Serena Energia (formerly Omega Energia) is a holding company whose main business is generating power from wind, solar and hydro assets in Brazil and the US, with energy trading on the side, so it fits Renewable Electricity; it moved from CVM Category A to B after a 2025 tender offer.

Hospital Anchieta S.A. owns and runs Hospital Anchieta, a general hospital in Taguatinga (DF) that belongs to the Kora Saúde hospital group, so its main business is running a hospital (Health Care Facilities).

Rumo Malha Central is the Rumo-group single-asset concessionaire holding the subconcession of the 1,537 km Ferrovia Norte-Sul central section (Porto Nacional/TO–Estrela D'Oeste/SP), where it operates rail freight transportation, fitting Rail Transportation consistent with parent Rumo S.A.

Lupo is a long-established manufacturer of socks, underwear and sportswear that sells mostly wholesale through multi-brand retailers (about 61% of 2020 net revenue), franchisees (about 22%) and department stores (about 14%), so it is an apparel manufacturer rather than a retailer, despite the CVM label "Comércio".

Asa Branca Holding is a holding company in the Essentia Energia group. Its only investment is the Asa Branca Wind Complex, five wind-farm SPEs (Asa Branca IV–VIII) in Rio Grande do Norte, so its business is renewable (wind) power generation.

Cerradinho Bioenergia (CerradinhoBio) gets most of its revenue from ethanol made from sugarcane and corn (865 thousand m³ in the 2025/26 crop year, of which 687 thousand m³ was corn ethanol), with sugar, DDGs, corn oil and cogenerated power as smaller lines, so it fits GICS Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, which explicitly includes ethanol producers.

Holding do Araguaia is a single-purpose holding (65% EcoRodovias / 35% GLP X) that owns 100% of Concessionária Ecovias do Araguaia, the toll-road concession for BR-153/414/080 in Tocantins and Goiás, so it is classified by the concession activity as Highways & Railtracks.

Ecovias do Cerrado is an EcoRodovias toll-road concession granted by ANTT. It operates the 437 km BR-364/365 highway system between Jataí (GO) and Uberlândia (MG), so as a single-asset road concession it belongs in Highways & Railtracks.

Aura Almas Mineração is the Aura Minerals subsidiary that owns and runs the Almas gold mine in Tocantins, which has been in commercial production since 2023. Gold mining is its main activity, so it fits Gold.

GSH Corp runs outsourced hemotherapy and hematology services (blood banks and transfusion services operated inside partner hospitals), plus nuclear medicine and radiopharmacy, across many branches in Brazil; these are patient health care services rather than owning hospitals, so it fits Health Care Services.

Auren is a holding company that controls CESP, the former Votorantim Energia assets and, since 2024, AES Brasil; its main business is hydro, wind and solar power generation (about 8.8 GW, making it the 3rd-largest generator in Brazil), along with a large energy-trading arm, so earnings and market perception point to Renewable Electricity.

Ecovias do Araguaia is an EcoRodovias toll-road concessionaire. It operates the Anápolis–Aliança do Tocantins system (BR-153, BR-414 and BR-080, about 850.7 km), so it fits as an owner and operator of roads under Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: TRANSMISSORA JOSÉ MARIA DE MACEDO DE ELETRICIDADE S.A.
rationale: This is a special-purpose company that holds an ANEEL electricity transmission concession (lines and substations) and is in its operational phase; GICS places electricity transmission companies in Electric Utilities.

company_name: ARGO V TRANSMISSAO DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Argo V (formerly Odoyá Transmissora) is a single-asset concession company whose corporate purpose is building, operating and maintaining a public electric power transmission service on the national grid's core network (Rede Básica do SIN), earning regulated RAP; under GICS, transmission belongs in Electric Utilities.

company_name: ARGO VI TRANSMISSAO DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Argo VI (formerly Esperanza Transmissora de Energia) is a single-asset company holding a 30-year ANEEL public-service concession for an operating electricity transmission line (operating licence since 2019), owned by Argo Energia; GICS puts electricity transmission in Electric Utilities.

company_name: FOZ DO RIO CLARO ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Foz do Rio Claro Energia is the special-purpose company (SPE) owning and operating the Foz do Rio Claro hydroelectric plant (UHE, ~68 MW) in Goiás, wholly owned by Alupar; its revenue comes from selling hydropower, so it is a Renewable Electricity producer.
Eurofarma is a large Brazilian pharmaceutical maker. It develops, makes and sells prescription, generic and OTC drugs in Brazil and Latin America, which fits the Pharmaceuticals sub-industry.

This is a special-purpose company that holds ANEEL transmission concession contract 010/2008 to build, operate and maintain the 500 kV Oriximiná–Silves–Lechuga line in Pará and Amazonas, so it is classified as electricity transmission (Electric Utilities).

Iguá Rio de Janeiro S.A. is the concessionaire for CEDAE Block 2 (Barra da Tijuca/Jacarepaguá and Miguel Pereira/Paty do Alferes), handling water distribution and sewage collection and treatment, so it fits Water Utilities.

Aegea-controlled SPE holding the Bloco 1 concession from the State of Rio de Janeiro (ex-CEDAE) for water supply and sewage services, a single-asset water/sanitation concession that fits Water Utilities.
Águas do Rio 4 SPE is Aegea's single-concession company running water supply and sewage services in CEDAE Block 4 of Rio de Janeiro under a 35-year contract, which fits Water Utilities.

company_name: TECIDOS E ARMARINHOS MIGUEL BARTOLOMEU S.A.
rationale: The company trades as Tambasa Atacadistas, a large wholesale distributor based in Contagem, MG, that sells mostly building materials, hardware, electrical and plumbing products to retailers, which fits Trading Companies & Distributors (B2B distribution of building products and electrical equipment) rather than consumer merchandise distribution. Second independent pass proposed 30101040 (Consumer Staples Merchandise Retail).

Senior Sistemas (Blumenau/SC) develops and licenses enterprise management software (ERP, HCM/payroll, logistics/WMS/TMS, CRM), mostly as SaaS/subscription and maintenance, which places it in Application Software.

Copel Distribuição is the ANEEL-concessioned public electricity distribution utility for nearly all of Paraná state (>206k km of distribution networks), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Copel, fitting Electric Utilities (electricity distribution).

CCR ViaCosteira is a single-asset toll road concessionaire that manages and operates 220.4 km of federal highway BR-101 in southern Santa Catarina (Palhoça to Passo de Torres) under an ANTT concession, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.
União Química makes human medicines (prescription, generics and OTC), plus veterinary drugs and contract manufacturing, so it fits Pharmaceuticals.

company_name: EIXO SP CONCESSIONARIA DE RODOVIAS S.A.
rationale: Eixo SP is a single-asset toll road concessionaire: under a 2020 contract with ARTESP, it runs the Piracicaba–Panorama (PiPa) highway lot in São Paulo state, so it falls under Highways & Railtracks.

IFIN is a special-purpose financing vehicle that used to be a credit securitizer (IFIN Companhia Securitizadora de Créditos Financeiros, linked to Virgo). It issued R$550m of debentures (IFPT11) to fund its main asset, about R$674m in preferred shares of and receivables from Camastra Participações, indexed to IPCA + 7.6% a year. That makes it a structured-finance vehicle best placed in Specialized Finance, even though the CVM status says pre-operational.

company_name: VIA BRASIL BR 163 CONCESSIONARIA DE RODOVIAS S.A.
rationale: Single-asset federal toll-road concessionaire operating and collecting tolls on ~1,009 km of BR-163/230 from Sinop (MT) to Miritituba (PA) under an ANTT contract. The CVM "pre-operational" status appears outdated, so the company is classified as a toll-road owner/operator under Highways & Railtracks.

Regenera Rio (formerly Ciclus Ambiental Rio/do Brasil, now controlled by Aegea) holds an administrative concession (PPP) with Comlurb for integrated municipal solid-waste management, operating the Seropédica waste treatment center (CTR) and transfer stations, which is waste management and fits Environmental & Facilities Services rather than a water/gas utility.

company_name: ELEA DIGITAL INFRAESTRUTURA E REDES DE TELECOMUNICAÇÕES S.A.
rationale: Elea Digital operates carrier-neutral data centers in Brazil, providing colocation, interconnection, connectivity and managed services to hyperscalers and corporates. Data center operators that are not REITs fit Internet Services & Infrastructure.

Oceânica provides offshore subsea services (diving, ROV operations, inspection and integrity maintenance of subsea assets) mainly to Petrobras, which makes it an oil & gas equipment and services provider.

Borrachas Vipal makes rubber products for tire retreading and repair (tread rubber, camelbacks, patches, cements) as well as tires and industrial rubber, which places it in the Tires & Rubber sub-industry.

company_name: BRK AMBIENTAL - REGIÃO METROPOLITANA DE MACEIÓ S.A.
rationale: BRK Maceió holds a 35-year concession to distribute water and collect and treat sewage in 10 municipalities of the Maceió metropolitan region, so it is a water utility.
Solar Bebidas is a Coca-Cola system bottler in Brazil that makes and distributes soft drinks and other non-alcoholic beverages, which fits Soft Drinks & Non-alcoholic Beverages.

company_name: V. TAL - REDE NEUTRA DE TELECOMUNICAÇÕES S.A.
rationale: V.tal (formerly BrT Multimídia, spun out of Oi and controlled by BTG Pactual) runs a neutral fiber-optic network. Its main business is wholesale fiber/FTTH capacity sold to carriers and ISPs, which fits Alternative Carriers; the recently acquired Nio (ex-Oi Fibra) retail broadband business adds some Integrated Telecom exposure.

Althaia is a Brazilian drugmaker whose main business is manufacturing generic, similar and OTC drugs, plus contract development and production for other pharma companies; this fits Pharmaceuticals, with supplements as a secondary line.

Orizon Meio Ambiente S.A. is the operating company of the Orizon Valorização de Resíduos group. Its CNPJ appears on the orizonvr.com.br site. The company runs waste treatment and recovery ecoparks and landfills, which earn most of its revenue, with smaller income from biogas, energy and carbon credits. Waste management falls under Environmental & Facilities Services rather than water or gas utilities.
Vitru Educação is a holding that controls the private higher-education institutions UNIASSELVI and UniCesumar, among Brazil's largest distance-learning (EAD) providers, so it fits Education Services.

company_name: COMPANHIA DO METROPOLITANO DE SÃO PAULO - METRÔ
rationale: São Paulo state-controlled Metrô operates the city's subway (metro rail) passenger lines; most of its revenue comes from fares (about 88% of gross operating revenue in 2021), which fits passenger rail transportation.

Solví Essencis Ambiental operates landfills and handles and treats municipal and industrial waste. Waste management falls under Environmental & Facilities Services, not Water Utilities, even though the CVM label says sanitation.

NSN ("Columbus", MLog group) is the shipping arm that collects, through an SCP, the results of offshore support vessels (AHTS/OSRV chartered to the oil industry, about R$52m of R$68m net revenue in 1Q24) and Amazon inland fuel barging by CNA (about R$16m), so offshore oil-and-gas support services are the dominant activity.

company_name: TIM BRASIL SERVIÇOS E PARTICIPAÇÕES S.A.
rationale: TIM Brasil Serviços e Participações is a non-operating holding company wholly owned by the Telecom Italia group whose sole purpose is to control TIM S.A., a Brazilian mobile carrier focused on wireless service, so as a single-business holding it takes TIM's Wireless Telecommunication Services classification.

company_name: CHINA THREE GORGES BRASIL ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: CTG Brasil is a holding/operating company of China Three Gorges whose dominant business is renewable power generation via 17 hydroelectric plants and 11 wind farms (~8.3 GW), Brazil's second-largest private generator, fitting Renewable Electricity.

Rio+ Saneamento BL3 is the Grupo Águas do Brasil concessionaire for Block 3 of the CEDAE auction. Under a 35-year concession, it provides water supply and sewage collection and treatment to about 2.6 million people in Rio de Janeiro State, which makes it a water utility.

company_name: COMPANHIA ESTADUAL DE GERAÇÃO DE ENERGIA ELÉTRICA - CEEE-G
rationale: CEEE-G is a Rio Grande do Sul power generator, now controlled by CSN, that operates only hydroelectric plants (5 large plants, 8 small plants and 2 micro plants, about 921 MW), so it fits Renewable Electricity.

Unidas Locadora S.A. (CNPJ 45.736.131/0001-70, Belo Horizonte, Brookfield-controlled) runs the Unidas car-rental (RAC) business carved out of the Localiza–Unidas merger, and GICS places vehicle rental in Passenger Ground Transportation.

Votorantim Cimentos is one of the world's largest cement producers, and its revenue comes mostly from cement, concrete, aggregates and mortar in Brazil, North America, Europe/Asia/Africa and Latin America, which places it in Construction Materials.
Turbi runs a 100% digital, app-based car-sharing and car-rental service in Brazil, renting cars by the hour, day or month. GICS puts vehicle rental under Passenger Ground Transportation.

Granja Faria is one of Brazil's largest egg producers; it produces and sells shell eggs and egg-derived products under its own brands (similar to Cal-Maine), so it fits Packaged Foods & Meats rather than unbranded Agricultural Products.

Origem Energia is a holding company whose main operating subsidiary, Origem Alagoas, produces onshore natural gas, condensate/LPG and oil in the Polo Alagoas fields it bought from Petrobras; most of its revenue comes from selling that oil and gas, which fits Oil & Gas Exploration & Production. Its gas storage and power projects are secondary.

company_name: VRENTAL LOCAÇÃO DE MÁQUINAS E EQUIPAMENTOS S.A.
rationale: VRENTAL is a publicly registered S.A. based in Indaiatuba/SP whose registered main activity (CNAE 77.32-2-01) is renting construction machinery and equipment without an operator, with branches in several states; GICS places industrial machinery rental to businesses in Trading Companies & Distributors.

CLI Sul is the Corredor Logística e Infraestrutura subsidiary that bought 80% of Elevações Portuárias from Rumo; it runs a leased agri-bulk export terminal for sugar and grains at the Port of Santos, which is port terminal operation (Marine Ports & Services).

Inspirali, controlled by Ânima Educação, runs a network of MEC-recognised private medical schools (about 15 schools and 15.7k students), so tuition from higher education is its main revenue, which fits Education Services.

CLI is an independent ("bandeira branca") port terminal operator providing grain elevation/port logistics to agribusiness trading companies at terminals in Itaqui (São Luís) and Santos, which fits owners/operators of marine ports and port support services.

company_name: CONCESSIONARIA ROTA DE SANTA MARIA S.A
rationale: Single-asset toll road concession operating the RSC-287 highway in Rio Grande do Sul, earning toll revenue regulated by AGERGS. GICS classes owners and operators of roads under Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: BRAZIL TOWER, CESSÃO DE INFRA-ESTRUTURAS S.A
rationale: Brazil Tower is a non-REIT telecom infrastructure company whose revenue comes mainly from leasing antenna space on the roughly 1,761 towers it builds and operates, and the GICS definition places companies that construct and operate telecom towers in Integrated Telecommunication Services.

Voke (formerly Agasus/Microcity) earns about 90% of its revenue from business-to-business rental of IT hardware (notebooks, desktops, smartphones) on a Hardware-as-a-Service basis, and the rest from selling used equipment; GICS treats B2B equipment rental like this as Trading Companies & Distributors, although IT Consulting & Other Services is a reasonable alternative. Second independent pass proposed 45102010 (IT Consulting & Other Services).
Holding/SPE owning the UFV Hélio Valgas photovoltaic solar plants, which ANEEL has authorized for commercial operation; its activity is solar electricity generation, so it fits Renewable Electricity.

Metrocasa is a São Paulo developer-builder (incorporadora and construtora) that builds and sells affordable residential apartments and studios to homebuyers, so it fits Homebuilding, consistent with how integrated Brazilian residential developer-builders are treated.

Águas do Sertão is the Conasa-controlled concessionaire for Alagoas sanitation Bloco B, providing water distribution and sewage collection to 34 municipalities. That makes it a single-activity water utility concession.

Ligga Telecomunicações (formerly Copel Telecom) earns most of its revenue (about R$610m LTM Mar-2025) from fixed fiber-optic broadband internet access to end users in Paraná, which makes it a fixed-line ISP under Integrated Telecommunication Services.

company_name: BRASIL BIOFUELS S.A. - EM RECUPERAÇÃO JUDICIAL
rationale: Brasil BioFuels is the holding company of the BBF group. The group grows palm on its own plantations and produces crude palm oil, which reportedly made up about 78.7% of revenue, compared with about 19.9% from thermal power plants in the North's isolated grids and about 1.2% from biodiesel, so it fits Agricultural Products & Services better than the CVM 'Energia Elétrica' label.

Let's Rent a Car is a Brazilian light-vehicle rental and corporate fleet-outsourcing company; vehicle rental falls under Passenger Ground Transportation, the same sub-industry as peers Localiza and Movida.

BRZ is a Belo Horizonte-based developer-builder (incorporadora/construtora) of low-income residential units under the Minha Casa Minha Vida program in southeastern Brazil, building and selling homes to individual buyers, consistent with Homebuilding (as with peers MRV, Direcional, Cury).

Concessionária ViaRio is a single-asset concession that runs the tolled TransOlímpica expressway (Corredor Tancredo Neves) in Rio de Janeiro and earns its revenue from tolls, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: CONCESSIONÁRIA DO SISTEMA RODOVIÁRIO RIO-SÃO PAULO S.A.
rationale: CCR RioSP (Motiva group) holds the ANTT federal toll-road concession for Via Dutra (BR-116) and Rio-Santos (BR-101), earning revenue from toll collection and highway operation, which fits Highways & Railtracks.

Alubar mainly makes bare and insulated aluminum electrical wires, cables and conductors for power transmission and distribution, and cable sales are the largest revenue line; its aluminum rod output mostly supplies its own cable plants, so it fits Electrical Components & Equipment (cables and wires) rather than Aluminum.

unclassified_reason: I couldn't verify the business: web search hit its usage limit before any results came back, so no primary source (IR site, CVM filings, regulator) was checked. The only evidence is the CVM sector label 'Saneamento, Serv. Água e Gás'. That label is a hint, not evidence, and it covers both water/sanitation and gas distribution. Parsan may also be a holding or financing vehicle (CNPJ registered around 2022, Category B). Assigning Water Utilities or Gas Utilities would be a guess.
rationale: No primary-source evidence was retrieved, and the coarse CVM label (water or gas, possibly a holding) is not enough to tell Water Utilities (55104010) apart from Gas Utilities (55102010) or a financial/holding vehicle. Second independent pass proposed 55104010 (Water Utilities).

EcoRioMinas (Ecovias Rio Minas), an EcoRodovias group company, holds the federal toll-road concession for BR-116 (RJ/MG), BR-465 and BR-493 (about 727 km); as a single-asset road concession it fits Highways & Railtracks.

company_name: CONCESSIONÁRIA DE RODOVIAS NOROESTE PAULISTA S.A
rationale: EcoNoroeste (now Ecovias Noroeste Paulista), an EcoRodovias subsidiary, holds and operates the Noroeste Paulista toll-road concession in São Paulo state, collecting tolls since 2023 — a single-asset highway concession fitting Highways & Railtracks.

AXIA Energia Norte (formerly Eletronorte, an Eletrobras/AXIA subsidiary) gets most of its revenue from generating power, mainly at large hydro plants (Tucuruí 8,370 MW, Teles Pires, Balbina, ~12.4 GW installed in total), so it fits Renewable Electricity, though it also has a large transmission business (~11,100 km of lines, 59 substations) and some gas-fired thermal plants.

AXIA Energia Sul (formerly CGT Eletrosul), an AXIA/Eletrobras subsidiary, mainly runs electricity transmission concessions in southern Brazil (main CNAE 3512300, transmission) and also has some hydro and wind generation, so it fits Electric Utilities, which covers transmission companies.

Brasil Tecnologia e Participações S.A. (Brasil TecPar) is a holding company that controls regional fiber-optic internet providers such as Amigo Telecom and Netell, which sell broadband and connectivity to homes and businesses, so it fits Integrated Telecommunication Services as an internet service provider to end users. This is based on prior knowledge and the CVM telecom label because web search was unavailable.

Giga Mais Fibra (Giga+ Fibra, part of the Alloha Fibra group) runs a fiber-optic broadband network and sells internet access to homes and businesses in Brazil, and GICS puts fixed-line ISPs serving end users in Integrated Telecommunication Services.

Vital Engenharia Ambiental provides outsourced urban cleaning services to municipalities, including waste collection, transport, treatment and final disposal, street sweeping, and building and running landfills, which makes it a waste-management business under Environmental & Facilities Services and not a water/gas utility as the CVM label suggests.

company_name: FISIA COMÉRCIO DE PRODUTOS ESPORTIVOS S.A.
rationale: Fisia is Nike's official distributor in Brazil, controlled by Grupo SBF; in 2024 about two-thirds of its R$5.1bn gross revenue came from direct-to-consumer channels (digital R$2.04bn and physical stores R$1.43bn) versus wholesale (R$1.64bn), so its main activity is retail of athletic footwear and apparel.
EPR Triângulo is a single-asset toll road concession (Grupo EPR) operating and maintaining 627.4 km of state highways in Triângulo Mineiro/Alto Paranaíba (MG), so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

This holding company exists to own the SPEs of Omega Energia's Assuruá 4 and Assuruá 5 wind farm complexes in Bahia, and its project-finance debentures fund them, so it is classified by the controlled activity: renewable (wind) power generation.

company_name: BELORA RDVC CITY DESENVOLVIMENTO IMOBILIÁRIO S.A.
